| `mss_translation_chunks_per_article` | histogram | chunks | none; buckets 1, 2, 3, 5, 10, 20 | worker | HP-2, FP-D4 |
| `mss_translation_input_tokens_total`, `mss_translation_output_tokens_total` | counter | tokens | `origin` (provider, mock, cache) | worker | HP-2, T-SLI-6 |
| `mss_translation_dead_total` | counter | jobs | `reason` (too_long, invalid_output, permanent, attempts, budget_never; 5) | worker finish | FP-2, FP-D1 |
| `mss_translation_enqueue_total` | counter | articles | `outcome` (queued, not_needed, no_content, lang_unknown) | ingest | FP-1, HP-1 |
| `mss_translation_coverage` | gauge | articles | `state` (translated, queued, running, deferred, dead, skipped) | status refresher (ledger query) | T-SLI-2, T-SLI-4 |
| `mss_translation_reconcile_mismatch_total` | counter | checks | none | hourly ledger check | FP-1, T-SLI-4 |
| `mss_translation_stale_current` | gauge | rows | none | ledger query: current translation where `article_version <> articles.version` | FP-6, FP-DB2 |
| `mss_translation_cache_rows`, `mss_translation_cache_oldest_age_seconds` | gauge | rows, s | none | sweeper | FP-DB5 |
| `mss_search_matches_total` | counter | results | `kind` (original, translation, both) | search route | ADR-0025, FP-S1 |
| `mss_search_foreign_untranslated` | gauge | articles | none (last computed value, refreshed every 60 s over all time, not per query) | status refresher | search coverage line |
| `mss_translation_view_total` | counter | events | `view` (translated, original) | beacon route (below) | usage of the reveal button |
| `mss_translation_page_state_total` | counter | pages | `state` (translated, pending, failed, deferred, not_needed) | article page server render | P3, UX honesty |
Existing series get new label values only: `mss_jobs{part="translation"}`, `mss_job_outcomes_total{part="translation"}`, `mss_job_oldest_age_seconds{part="translation"}`, `mss_db_query_duration_seconds{query="translation_save"}` and `{query="search_translation_exists"}`, `mss_breaker_state{provider="openai-translate"}` (the translate breaker name from architect 0003 section 8; extend `worker_set_flag` key `breaker.openai-translate`, already allowed by the `breaker.%` rule).

## 5. Logs
Structured events, level `info` unless noted; all carry `article_id`, `article_version`, `job_id`, `part="translation"`, `language` (as stored), `build`, `prompt_version`. Never the text, headline, chunk content, or the model output (extends redaction test).
| Event | Level | Extra fields |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `translation.enqueued` | debug | `outcome` (sampled 1%) |
| `translation.chunk_rejected` | warn | `chunk_idx`, `reason`, `len_in`, `len_out`, `ratio`, `script`, `detected_lang` |
| `translation.accepted` | info | `chunk_count`, `input_tokens`, `output_tokens`, `cost_micro`, `trust`, `flags[]`, `cache_hits`, `duration_ms` |
| `translation.dead` | warn | `reason`, `attempts`, `last_error` (existing safe formatter) |
| `translation.superseded` | info | `job_version`, `article_version` (late result discarded) |
| `translation.injection_flag` | warn | `chunk_idx`, `trust="low"` (also increments the existing counter) |
Decision records (P7): `translation.accepted` is the record that links an article to the model, prompt version and flags; the same data sits in `enrichments`, so a developer can answer "why does this article show this translation" from one log line plus the `/api/articles/:id/trace` JSON, which gains the translation row (UX/plan item).

## 6. Traces
Span `translation.job` (parent) with children `translation.chunk` (attrs: `idx`, `tokens_in`, `tokens_out`, `cache_hit`, `outcome`) and `translation.save` (DB). Search spans gain attribute `search.translation_side=true` when the EXISTS branch is present. Sampling: head 1% baseline (existing), keep 100% of jobs that end `dead`, `rejected`, or exceed 5 minutes (tail rule, if the stack supports it; otherwise log only, UNCONFIRMED).

## 7. Request and response times
| Interface | Metric | Buckets | Notes |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| OpenAI translate call (per chunk) | `mss_provider_duration_seconds{provider="openai-translate"}` (existing histogram, new value) | 0.5 to 60 s | timeout per chunk from config; per-job deadline logged |
| Article page | `mss_http_request_duration_seconds{route="article"}` | existing | one extra indexed lookup; watch for regression |
| Search | `mss_search_duration_seconds` with `kind` unchanged, plus plan experiment baseline | existing | T-SLI-5 |
| `POST /api/telemetry/translation-view` | `mss_http_request_duration_seconds{route="ui_event"}` | existing | fire-and-forget |

## 8. Reveal-button usage event
Browser telemetry does not exist, so add the smallest thing that works: the client component posts `{view: "translated"|"original"}` with `navigator.sendBeacon` to `POST /api/telemetry/translation-view`. The route validates the enum, ignores everything else, increments `mss_translation_view_total{view}`, returns 204, writes nothing to the database, and is rate-limited per process (e.g. 20/s, over that it drops and counts `mss_ui_event_dropped_total`). No article id, user id or text is sent, so there is nothing personal to retain. Cost: one tiny route; benefit: tells whether readers trust or distrust translations (share of page views that click "show original"). Optional: can be dropped without affecting the feature. UNCONFIRMED whether the user wants it.

## 9. Alerts and runbook pointers
| ID | Condition | Severity | First check |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| T1 | share of jobs within 30 min below 95% over 6 h, or `mss_job_oldest_age_seconds{part="translation",state="queued"}` above 1 h | Ticket | breaker `openai-translate`, budget deferrals (`mss_budget_deferred_total`), worker concurrency |
| T2 | `mss_translation_coverage{state="dead"}` rising for 3 h, or coverage ratio below 98% | Ticket | `mss_translation_dead_total` by reason; `too_long` means raise the chunk cap or accept |
| T3 | rejected chunk share above 5% over 1 h, any `script` | Warn | `mss_translation_chunks_total` by reason and script; recent prompt or model change; sample a few chunks from logs (lengths only) |
| T4 | `increase(mss_translation_reconcile_mismatch_total[1h]) > 0` | Page | ledger query: foreign articles with no translation job; check the `isEnglish` rule and `ingest_new_version` parameter (FP-DB1) |
| T5 | search p95 above 1 s or 25% above baseline for 30 min | Warn | `kind` split, plan for `search_translation_exists`, GIN pending list size |
| T6 | `mss_translation_stale_current > 0` for 10 min | Ticket | version check in the save path; advisory lock (DBA section 8) |
| T7 | `mss_translation_cache_oldest_age_seconds` above 10 days | Ticket | sweeper |
| T8 | injection flag rate on translation inputs above 5× the 7-day baseline | Warn | source breakdown in logs; possible attack on a source |
Breaker open for `openai-translate` is covered by the existing breaker-open alert once the name is added to `ops/alerts.yml`.

## 10. Dashboards
Infra view (new row "Translation"): lag p50/p95/p99 (T-SLI-1), coverage by state (stacked), queue age, spend share against the cap, breaker state, search p95 with `kind` split.
Developer view (new row): rejection reasons by script, chunks per article, tokens per article, last 20 `translation.dead` and `translation.chunk_rejected` log lines (lengths and reasons only), lookup by article id showing page state, translation row, job trail. Product row: `translated` versus `original` view clicks, page state mix (how often readers see "pending").

## 11. Overhead and cardinality budget
- All new labels are bounded (largest series: chunks `outcome × reason × script` = 3 × 7 × 4, in practice far fewer). No `source`, `language` (raw), `article_id` or text as labels; `language` and `source` live in logs and span attributes.
- Volume: translation events are per foreign article, not per ingested article. At 800/s with 10% foreign: 80 jobs/s, about 4 chunks each, so about 320 `translation.chunk_*` counter increments/s (in-process, negligible); logs only on rejection, dead, accepted: about 80 lines/s at 10% foreign, roughly 300 bytes each, about 2 GB/day. At PoC volume (50,000/day) it is a few MB. Sample `translation.accepted` to 10% above 20 jobs/s (config) to keep the 800/s case near 0.2 GB/day. UNCONFIRMED against the actual log retention.
- Ledger gauges (`coverage`, `stale_current`, `foreign_untranslated`) run one grouped query each every 60 s on the read pool, using the partial indexes (DBA 0003 section 7). Verify each stays under 200 ms at 1M rows.

## 12. Coverage of the architect registers
| ID | Signal |
| --- | --- |
| FP-1 | `mss_translation_enqueue_total`, T4 reconciliation |
| FP-2 | `mss_translation_coverage{state}`, `mss_translation_dead_total`, `mss_translation_page_state_total` |
| FP-3 | `mss_translation_chunks_total{reason="mismatch"}` |
| FP-4 | `reason="echo"`, `reason="wrong_lang"` |
| FP-5, FP-D1 | `mss_prompt_injection_suspected_total`, `reason="injected"`, T8 |
| FP-6, FP-DB2, FP-S2 | `mss_translation_stale_current`, T6 |
| FP-7 | no metric (rendering); covered by Playwright test in the testing spec |
| FP-8 | `mss_budget_deferred_total`, spend share T-SLI-6 |
| FP-9 | `lang_unknown` outcome in `mss_translation_enqueue_total`; language-mix sampling is a manual audit |
| FP-10, FP-S1, FP-S3 | `mss_search_matches_total{kind}` (a zero `translation` share while translations exist), tests |
| FP-D2, FP-D3 | chunk rejection share by script (T3) |
| FP-D4 | `mss_translation_chunks_total{outcome="cache_hit"}`, chunks per article, tokens |
| FP-DB3 | migration lock time (measured in test, not production metric) |
| FP-DB4, FP-S4, HP-S1, HP-DB2 | T5, `mss_db_query_duration_seconds{query="search_translation_exists"}` |
| FP-DB5 | cache gauges, T7 |
| HP-1, HP-DB1 | existing `mss_ingest_duration_seconds` (compare with and without the enqueue branch in the benchmark) |
| HP-2 | tokens and cost histograms |
| HP-3 | article route duration |
| HP-D1 | `mss_translation_validate_seconds` histogram (add, buckets 1 ms to 1 s) |

## 13. Implementation notes for the plan
- Benchmark and tests can read the ledger directly: `enrichment_jobs` where `part = 'translation'` by state, `article_translations` current rows, and the counters above through `/api/metrics`. No extra instrumentation is needed for completeness checks.
- Order of work: (1) add label keys `script`, `view` to the allow-list and the catalogue test; (2) enqueue and worker counters; (3) validators' reason counters; (4) ledger gauges and reconcile check; (5) page state counter and beacon route; (6) alert rules and Grafana row; (7) redaction test update for translation fields.
- carma-devops: no new service; add the alert rules and dashboard JSON to `ops/` so `docker compose up` provisions them; add `breaker.openai-translate` handling in `ops/alerts.yml`.
- Note the in-process registry resets on restart and is per process (`globalThis.__mssMetrics`); ledger-derived gauges are therefore computed from the database rather than accumulated in memory.

## 14. Decisions needed and open questions
- Proposed SLO numbers (30 min/6 h lag, 98% coverage, 5% rejection) are placeholders, UNCONFIRMED.
- Reveal-button beacon: build it or skip (section 8)? Default: build, it is small. UNCONFIRMED.
- Log sampling of `translation.accepted` above 20 jobs/s and log retention. UNCONFIRMED.
- Tail sampling for traces depends on the existing stack's capability. UNCONFIRMED.

# carma-ux

The PoC is an internal tool. Its users are analysts and operators who work under time pressure, who must judge how far to trust every number, and who read in several scripts and directions. The interface carries Carma's principles to the person: it is where "every insight carries a confidence" (P6) either shows or does not.

The output is a specification a designer or design agent can turn into wireframes. It is not a visual design, and it prescribes behaviour and content, not colours or styling. Share the specification as is with the design handoff skills when they are available.

Read `references/carma-context.md` first for the principles, constraints and spec conventions.

## Inputs

Read the latest non-superseded `.specs/architect/NNNN-*.md` for the feature, and any `.specs/search/`, `.specs/telemetry/` and `.specs/data/dba/` specs for it, since they define what data and signals exist to be shown. Take from them: the data available per item (and its confidence and lineage fields), the states an item moves through, freshness and coverage signals, and search capabilities. A screen that needs data nobody produces is a defect in the plan, so note any such gap.

Inspect the codebase for existing front end: framework, component library, design tokens, existing pages and patterns, accessibility setup, localisation and RTL support. Reuse what exists. Record paths. If there is no front end, say so.

## Workflow

### 1. Identify the users and their core intents

Name the user roles (for example analyst, infra operator, developer debugging a case) and, for each, the intents the feature serves, phrased as what the person is trying to accomplish ("find every mention of a brand in the last hour and judge whether it is reliable"). Rank them: the primary intent decides the layout, and secondary intents must not compete with it.

If intent is unclear, or two intents pull the interface in opposite directions, do not guess. Ask, using the protocol in the context file. Typical questions: who is the main user, what decision are they making when they open this screen, is scanning speed or depth of inspection more important, what must be reachable in one click.

### 2. Explore approaches

Brainstorm at least two ways to present the feature, for example a ranked feed versus a faceted search workspace, an alert-first view versus a query-first view. Compare them against the primary intent and the principles, and recommend one with reasons. Where the choice is a genuine trade-off, put it to the user.

### 3. Apply the Carma interface principles

These recur on every screen, so state how each is met rather than leaving them to the designer's memory:

- **Confidence by default (P6).** Every derived value (sentiment, relevance, topic, summary, entity match) shows its confidence as a 0 to 100% figure next to it. Users may collapse the display but cannot lose sight that it exists. Where there is no confidence, say "no confidence available" instead of leaving a blank. Do not rely on colour alone to convey confidence.
- **"Why this number?" (P7).** Any confidence opens an explanation: origin (model self-report, rule, classifier, human review, combined), method and version, the raw value and range, normalised value. A self-reported model confidence is labelled as that, never as a probability.
- **Trace to source (P8).** Every insight and summary links to the articles it came from, and every article shows the original text and what was done to it (translated, summarised, classified, merged as a duplicate).
- **Honest freshness and coverage (P1, P3).** Show how fresh the data is (the index watermark) and what is covered. Design three distinct empty states: no match, not covered, not yet processed. Mark items that missed the 15-minute target as late instead of hiding them.
- **Signal first (P4, P10).** Lead with the relevant and the explained; keep raw detail one step behind a summary. Removed or merged content (duplicates, filtered items) is recoverable and visibly accounted for.
- **Language and direction (P5).** Right-to-left layouts, mixed-direction text within one line, Chinese text without spaces, correct fonts per script, language labels, and search behaviour that works across scripts. Specify how text direction is determined per item and how mixed content is isolated so it cannot garble neighbouring elements.
- **Human and automated (P9).** Each derived value is marked automated, human-reviewed or human-authored, and the interface offers a path to review, correct or override where the architect placed a human touchpoint.
- **Built for scanning (P11).** Dense but legible, keyboard-friendly, fast to the answer; alerts that interrupt only when they should.

### 4. Specify pages, components and flows

For each page: its purpose and primary intent, the content and its priority, the components used, the data fields required (with the source spec), interactions, and the full set of states, including loading, empty (the three kinds), partial data (some stages not finished), stale data, error, and permission or quota limits. Specify what is shown at 800 articles a second in a live view: how updates are paced so the screen is readable, what pauses, what is aggregated.

For each component: name, purpose, variants, props or inputs, states, and accessibility notes. Reuse existing components where the codebase has them and flag new ones.

Describe the key flows end to end (for example from an alert to the source article to a correction), with the decision points.

Include accessibility expectations (keyboard operation, screen reader labels, contrast, focus order, reduced motion) and responsive expectations where relevant.

### 5. Wireframe brief

Write a short brief for the designer or design agent: what to wireframe first, the layout hierarchy per page (what sits where and why, in words or a simple text sketch), and the questions the wireframes should answer. State the fidelity expected (low-fidelity structure and content, not visual polish).

### 6. Decisions to put to the user

Raise choices that need a human: the primary user and intent where unclear, density versus simplicity, how prominent confidence is, how live views update, and which screens are in the PoC. Use the protocol in the context file.

## Output

Write the spec with these sections:

1. **Summary**
2. **Users and core intents** (ranked; primary intent marked)
3. **Approaches considered** (options, trade-offs, recommendation)
4. **Information architecture** (pages and how they connect)
5. **Page specifications** (per page as described above, with states)
6. **Component specifications** (reuse versus new)
7. **Key flows**
8. **Principle compliance** (table: principle, how the interface meets it, where)
9. **Data requirements** (every field the interface needs, which spec provides it, gaps)
10. **Accessibility and internationalisation**
11. **Wireframe brief** (for the designer or design agent)
12. **Decisions needed and open questions**

## Persisting the work (when run inside a codebase)

Follow "Spec conventions" in the context file. Number with `python scripts/next_spec_number.py .specs/ux`, write `.specs/ux/NNNN-<feature-slug>.md` with `spec: carma-ux` front matter and list the architect spec under `inputs`. Edit in place while `draft`. When the user decides a question that should be binding, suggest recording it as an ADR through carma-architect.

If you are not in a codebase, deliver the output in the conversation and offer to save it.


ARGUMENTS: Feature slug: article-translation. Repo root D:\Dev\Carma\interview. Inputs: .specs/architect/0003-article-translation.md, ADRs 0015, 0016, 0022-0025, .specs/search/0002-article-translation.md (search covers original and translated text; matched_in marker; not-translated coverage line), .specs/data/sanitization/0003-article-translation.md (page states, trust=low banner, XSS rule: text only), .specs/data/dba/0003-article-translation.md, .specs/telemetry/0003-article-translation.md (page state counter, reveal beacon), and existing .specs/ux/0001 and 0002 plus the wireframe in .specs/ux/wireframes for conventions and the actual code under src/app/articles/[id], src/components (TextBlock, ArticleCard, search/*). Decisions already made; do not re-ask. Specify: article page default translated view with 'Machine translated from <language>' label, 'Show original' / 'Show translation' toggle (accessible, keyboard, aria-pressed, no layout jump, both texts in the HTML, per-block lang/dir for RTL and CJK), headline treatment, all page states (translated, pending, deferred for budget, failed/too_long, not needed/English, trust=low warning), search results card 'matched in translation' marker and the standing note on not-yet-translated foreign articles, mobile layout, copy text. The user can be asked only if intent is truly unclear. Write the next numbered spec in .specs/ux/.

# 0003 Translated article view with reveal-original, and search markers

## 1. Summary
For a non-English article, the article page shows the English translation of headline and body by default, labelled as machine translation, with one toggle to show the original and back. The original is always one click away and never removed (P8). Every state where a translation is not available says so in words and shows the original instead (P3). Search results gain a "matched in translation" marker and a standing note about foreign articles not translated yet. No confidence is shown for translations; the interface says "no confidence available" in the explanation (ADR-0024, P6, P7).

## 2. Users and core intents
| Role | Intent | Rank |
| --- | --- | --- |
| Analyst | Read what a foreign article says without leaving the page, and judge whether the translation can be trusted | Primary |
| Analyst | Check the original wording (a quote, a brand name, a figure) | Primary |
| Analyst | Find a foreign article by an English term or an original-language term | Secondary (search) |
| Operator / developer | See why an article has no translation (pending, paused, failed) | Secondary |
The primary intent is reading, so the layout puts the translated text first and the check-the-original action next to it.

## 3. Approaches considered
| Option | For | Against |
| --- | --- | --- |
| A. Toggle that swaps one text block (recommended, as requested) | One column, no layout jump if sized sensibly, clear default, simple on mobile | Cannot compare line by line |
| B. Side by side | Easy comparison | Needs width, poor on mobile, doubles reading effort, no toggle as asked |
| C. Inline paragraph reveal | Fine-grained check | Complex, hides context, harder for RTL |
Recommendation: A. A "side by side" view is a possible later addition and is not designed here.

## 4. Information architecture
No new pages. Changed: `/articles/[id]` (`src/app/articles/[id]/page.tsx`), search results cards (`src/components/ArticleCard.tsx`, used by `src/components/search/SearchPage.tsx`), and the search page coverage area (`src/components/CoverageLine.tsx` neighbourhood). The trace JSON (`/api/articles/:id/trace`) gains the translation row (no UI change).

## 5. Page specification: article page `/articles/[id]`
Purpose: read and verify one article. Primary intent: read the translation, with a quick path to the original.

Layout, top to bottom (existing sections after "Text" are unchanged):
1. **Header.** Headline, then the metadata line (source, language, published, id, version). The headline follows the view: translated headline in translated view, original headline in original view. Metadata line gains the language as a readable name ("Arabic (ar)") instead of only the code.
2. **Translation bar** (new, directly under the header, above the text; only for articles that need translation):
   - Left: label "Machine translated from Arabic" (language name from the stored code; if unknown, "Machine translated"). When showing the original, the label reads "Original text (Arabic)".
   - Right: the toggle button, text "Show original" in translated view and "Show translation" in original view. Same position in both views.
   - Secondary line (muted): "Automated translation, not reviewed by a person. No confidence score is available." with a small "About this" disclosure explaining: model name and prompt version, when it was produced, trust flag if any, that the original is the system of record. This is the P7 "why" and reads from the `enrichments` row.
3. **Text.** One text region for the active view. Both texts are in the page HTML; the inactive one is hidden, so switching needs no request.
4. Existing sections: version list, derived values, transformations, processing trail. The processing trail gains a line "Job translation: succeeded · attempts 1" like the other jobs, and the enrichment line shows provider/model/origin/trust.

### Toggle behaviour
- One `<button type="button">`, with `aria-pressed` true while the original is shown, and `aria-controls` pointing at the text region. Visible label changes with the state; the accessible name stays "Show original text" / "Show translation" so screen readers hear the action.
- Keyboard: reachable in the tab order immediately after the page heading, activates with Enter and Space. Focus stays on the button after activation. After a switch, a polite live region announces "Showing original text (Arabic)" or "Showing English translation".
- Default is the translation whenever a valid current translation exists. Not remembered between articles or visits in the first version (the original is a deliberate check, not a preference). Optional later: remember per browser session. UNCONFIRMED.
- No layout jump: the text region keeps its minimum height from the taller of the two blocks (render both, hide one with a visually-hidden-but-measurable approach or set `min-height` from the longer one); the translation bar does not move. Scroll position is kept. On an article longer than one screen the toggle may scroll out of view, so it also appears as a compact sticky button at the top edge of the text region on scroll (UNCONFIRMED; default: show the bar again at the end of the text with the same button).
- Direction and language per block (P5): translated block `lang="en"`, `dir="ltr"`; original block `lang` = stored language, `dir="auto"` with bidi isolation (existing `TextBlock`). Headline and body each carry their own attributes. The metadata line and the toggle stay in the page's own direction. The `<title>` of the page uses the headline of the default view.

Primary intent: find articles, then decide which to open. The change is small.

2. **Card headline stays in the original language** (ADR-0025 scope). If there is no translated headline, the line is omitted. This single line is the only translated text on the list; cards otherwise remain original-language. # 0003 Translated article view with reveal-original, and search markers

## 1. Summary
For a non-English article, the article page shows the English translation of headline and body by default, labelled as machine translation, with one toggle to show the original and back. The original is always one click away and never removed (P8). Every state where a translation is not available says so in words and shows the original instead (P3). Search results gain a "matched in translation" marker and a standing note about foreign articles not translated yet. No confidence is shown for translations; the interface says "no confidence available" in the explanation (ADR-0024, P6, P7).

## 2. Users and core intents
| Role | Intent | Rank |
| --- | --- | --- |
| Analyst | Read what a foreign article says without leaving the page, and judge whether the translation can be trusted | Primary |
| Analyst | Check the original wording (a quote, a brand name, a figure) | Primary |
| Analyst | Find a foreign article by an English term or an original-language term | Secondary (search) |
| Operator / developer | See why an article has no translation (pending, paused, failed) | Secondary |
The primary intent is reading, so the layout puts the translated text first and the check-the-original action next to it.

## 3. Approaches considered
| Option | For | Against |
| --- | --- | --- |
| A. Toggle that swaps one text block (recommended, as requested) | One column, no layout jump if sized sensibly, clear default, simple on mobile | Cannot compare line by line |
| B. Side by side | Easy comparison | Needs width, poor on mobile, doubles reading effort, no toggle as asked |
| C. Inline paragraph reveal | Fine-grained check | Complex, hides context, harder for RTL |
Recommendation: A. A "side by side" view is a possible later addition and is not designed here.

## 4. Information architecture
No new pages. Changed: `/articles/[id]` (`src/app/articles/[id]/page.tsx`), search results cards (`src/components/ArticleCard.tsx`, used by `src/components/search/SearchPage.tsx`), and the search page coverage area (`src/components/CoverageLine.tsx` neighbourhood). The trace JSON (`/api/articles/:id/trace`) gains the translation row (no UI change).

## 5. Page specification: article page `/articles/[id]`

2. **Translation bar** (new, directly under the header, above the text; only for articles that need translation):

   - Right: the toggle button, text "Show original" in translated view and "Show translation" in original view. Same position in both views.
   - Secondary line (muted): "Automated translation, not reviewed by a person. No confidence score is available." with a small "About this" disclosure explaining: model name and prompt version, when it was produced, trust flag if any, that the original is the system of record. This is the P7 "why" and reads from the `enrichments` row.
3. **Text.** One text region for the active view. Both texts are in the page HTML; the inactive one is hidden, so switching needs no request.
4. Existing sections: version list, derived values, transformations, processing trail. The processing trail gains a line "Job translation: succeeded · attempts 1" like the other jobs, and the enrichment line shows provider/model/origin/trust.

Scroll position is kept. On an article longer than one screen the toggle may scroll out of view, so it also appears as a compact sticky button at the top edge of the text region on scroll (UNCONFIRMED; default: show the bar again at the end of the text with the same button).

Headline and body each carry their own attributes. The metadata line and the toggle stay in the page's own direction. - Text is rendered as text only. No Markdown, no links, no HTML from the model output (data-sanity 0003 section 7). Paragraphs preserved with `whitespace-pre-wrap`.
- A small client component, `TranslatedText` (below), owns the toggle; the page stays a server component and passes both texts as props. Check `node_modules/next/dist/docs/` for client component rules before coding, per `AGENTS.md`.
- The toggle click sends the usage beacon (`view` only) per telemetry 0003 section 8; failure of the beacon is silent.

If the translation has no headline but the original has one (translation row without `headline_en`), show the original headline with a muted note "Headline not translated". The `<title>` of the page uses the headline of the default view.

| `matched_in` and `headline_en` per search result | card marker and English line | search 0002 | search route must return both |
| Untranslated counts {queued, paused, failed} for the selection | standing note | search 0002 section 10 | new aggregate query, not yet specified in SQL (plan task) |
| Language display name from code | label | none | need a small code-to-name map (`Intl.DisplayNames` in the browser/server, falls back to the code) |

## 12. Accessibility and internationalisation
- Toggle is a real button with a visible focus ring, 44 px minimum touch target on mobile, `aria-pressed`, live region announcement; text is not colour-only for any state or warning.
- Contrast follows the existing tokens; the warn colour pairs with an icon and text.
- Reduced motion: no animation on the swap (an instant switch, no fade).
- Screen readers: each text block has a visible heading or `aria-label` ("English translation", "Original text, Arabic") and its `lang` attribute so the correct voice is used.
- Mobile (360 px wide): the bar stacks: label on the first line, button below at full width; the metadata line wraps; text is one column with the existing 16 px gutter; the sticky mini button is optional. Long Arabic and CJK lines wrap without horizontal scroll.
- Print and copy: copying text copies the visible view only.
- UI strings are English now, kept in `strings` for later translation of the interface itself (P5).

## 13. Wireframe brief
Wireframe at low fidelity: (1) article page, Arabic article, translated view with the bar; (2) the same page in original view (RTL block); (3) the same page with each non-happy state (pending, paused, failed, low trust, English article with no bar); (4) a search results page with one translation match card, one original match card, and the standing note; (5) the 360 px mobile version of (1). Questions to answer: does the toggle sit well above long text, does the page jump on swap, is "Machine translated" visible without scrolling, does the English headline line on cards add clutter, and can the "About this" disclosure be found without competing with the text.

## 14. Decisions needed and open questions
- Cards: show the "English: ..." headline line on every foreign card, or only on translation matches? Recommended: every foreign card that has a translation (helps scanning), UNCONFIRMED. This goes beyond ADR-0024/0025's display scope and would need the user's OK.
- Sticky toggle for long articles: default end-of-text repeat; sticky is optional, UNCONFIRMED.
- Remember "show original" per session: not in the first version.
- The `NOT` echo wording follows the search-spec default and is UNCONFIRMED.
- Side-by-side view: out of scope for now.

# 0003 Translated article view with reveal-original, and search markers

## 1. Summary
For a non-English article, the article page shows the English translation of headline and body by default, labelled as machine translation, with one toggle to show the original and back. The original is always one click away and never removed (P8). Every state where a translation is not available says so in words and shows the original instead (P3). Search results gain a "matched in translation" marker and a standing note about foreign articles not translated yet. No confidence is shown for translations; the interface says "no confidence available" in the explanation (ADR-0024, P6, P7).

## 2. Users and core intents
| Role | Intent | Rank |
| --- | --- | --- |
| Analyst | Read what a foreign article says without leaving the page, and judge whether the translation can be trusted | Primary |
| Analyst | Check the original wording (a quote, a brand name, a figure) | Primary |
| Analyst | Find a foreign article by an English term or an original-language term | Secondary (search) |
| Operator / developer | See why an article has no translation (pending, paused, failed) | Secondary |
The primary intent is reading, so the layout puts the translated text first and the check-the-original action next to it.

## 3. Approaches considered
| Option | For | Against |
| --- | --- | --- |
| A. Toggle that swaps one text block (recommended, as requested) | One column, no layout jump if sized sensibly, clear default, simple on mobile | Cannot compare line by line |
| B. Side by side | Easy comparison | Needs width, poor on mobile, doubles reading effort, no toggle as asked |
| C. Inline paragraph reveal | Fine-grained check | Complex, hides context, harder for RTL |
Recommendation: A. A "side by side" view is a possible later addition and is not designed here.

## 4. Information architecture
No new pages. Changed: `/articles/[id]` (`src/app/articles/[id]/page.tsx`), search results cards (`src/components/ArticleCard.tsx`, used by `src/components/search/SearchPage.tsx`), and the search page coverage area (`src/components/CoverageLine.tsx` neighbourhood). The trace JSON (`/api/articles/:id/trace`) gains the translation row (no UI change).

## 5. Page specification: article page `/articles/[id]`
Purpose: read and verify one article. Primary intent: read the translation, with a quick path to the original.

Layout, top to bottom (existing sections after "Text" are unchanged):
1. **Header.** Headline, then the metadata line (source, language, published, id, version). The headline follows the view: translated headline in translated view, original headline in original view. Metadata line gains the language as a readable name ("Arabic (ar)") instead of only the code.
2. **Translation bar** (new, directly under the header, above the text; only for articles that need translation):
   - Left: label "Machine translated from Arabic" (language name from the stored code; if unknown, "Machine translated"). When showing the original, the label reads "Original text (Arabic)".
   - Right: the toggle button, text "Show original" in translated view and "Show translation" in original view. Same position in both views.
   - Secondary line (muted): "Automated translation, not reviewed by a person. No confidence score is available." with a small "About this" disclosure explaining: model name and prompt version, when it was produced, trust flag if any, that the original is the system of record. This is the P7 "why" and reads from the `enrichments` row.
3. **Text.** One text region for the active view. Both texts are in the page HTML; the inactive one is hidden, so switching needs no request.
4. Existing sections: version list, derived values, transformations, processing trail. The processing trail gains a line "Job translation: succeeded · attempts 1" like the other jobs, and the enrichment line shows provider/model/origin/trust.

### Toggle behaviour
- One `<button type="button">`, with `aria-pressed` true while the original is shown, and `aria-controls` pointing at the text region. Visible label changes with the state; the accessible name stays "Show original text" / "Show translation" so screen readers hear the action.
- Keyboard: reachable in the tab order immediately after the page heading, activates with Enter and Space. Focus stays on the button after activation. After a switch, a polite live region announces "Showing original text (Arabic)" or "Showing English translation".
- Default is the translation whenever a valid current translation exists. Not remembered between articles or visits in the first version (the original is a deliberate check, not a preference). Optional later: remember per browser session. UNCONFIRMED.
- No layout jump: the text region keeps its minimum height from the taller of the two blocks (render both, hide one with a visually-hidden-but-measurable approach or set `min-height` from the longer one); the translation bar does not move. Scroll position is kept. On an article longer than one screen the toggle may scroll out of view, so it also appears as a compact sticky button at the top edge of the text region on scroll (UNCONFIRMED; default: show the bar again at the end of the text with the same button).
- Direction and language per block (P5): translated block `lang="en"`, `dir="ltr"`; original block `lang` = stored language, `dir="auto"` with bidi isolation (existing `TextBlock`). Headline and body each carry their own attributes. The metadata line and the toggle stay in the page's own direction. For an RTL original, the original block is right-aligned inside the same column; the toggle does not move.
- Fonts: the existing stack covers Arabic and CJK (`--font-sans` in `globals.css`); CJK text uses no word-spacing assumptions and wraps by character.
- Text is rendered as text only. No Markdown, no links, no HTML from the model output (data-sanity 0003 section 7). Paragraphs preserved with `whitespace-pre-wrap`.
- A small client component, `TranslatedText` (below), owns the toggle; the page stays a server component and passes both texts as props. Check `node_modules/next/dist/docs/` for client component rules before coding, per `AGENTS.md`.
- The toggle click sends the usage beacon (`view` only) per telemetry 0003 section 8; failure of the beacon is silent.

### Headline treatment
Both headlines come from the same row: `headline_en` and `articles.headline`. If the original has no headline, show the existing "(no headline)" placeholder in both views. If the translation has no headline but the original has one (translation row without `headline_en`), show the original headline with a muted note "Headline not translated". The `<title>` of the page uses the headline of the default view.

### States (page)
| State | What the reader sees | Notes |
| --- | --- | --- |
| Translated (default) | Section 5 layout | counter `page_state=translated` |
| Translated, low trust | Same, plus a warning line in the bar: "This text contained instruction-like content, so the translation may be unreliable." Warn colour, icon and text, not colour alone | `trust = 'low'`, ADR-0012 pattern, matches the existing "Possible prompt injection" badge |
| Pending | Original shown. Bar label: "Translation in progress. Showing the original." No toggle button (nothing to switch to). Muted "Check back shortly." | job queued/running/failed_retryable |
| Paused (budget) | Original shown. "Translation paused: the daily translation budget is used up. It will continue automatically." | job `deferred_budget`; reuses wording of the card's "Enrichment paused: daily budget reached" |
| Failed | Original shown. "Translation unavailable." plus a reason in plain words: "The text was too long to translate" (`too_long`), "The translation did not pass quality checks" (invalid output), "The translation service rejected the request" (permanent). Link "Details" to the processing trail anchor | job `dead` |
| No content | Nothing to translate: "No text to translate." | `skipped_no_content` |
| Not needed | English article: no translation bar, no toggle, unchanged page | language `en`/`en-*` |
| Unknown language | Treated as needs translation. If the model reports English, the bar says "This article looks like English; no translation needed." and shows the original | `lang_unknown` flag |
| Loading / error loading translation | The page is server rendered; a database failure for the translation query shows the original and "Translation could not be loaded." (never a blank) | |
Rule: the page never shows the original text labelled as a translation, and never shows a half-translated text (data-sanity: partial translations are not stored).

## 6. Page specification: search results
Primary intent: find articles, then decide which to open. The change is small.

1. **Match marker on each card** when the match came from the translation: a small tag "Matched in translation" next to the language tag; "Matched in original and translation" for both; no tag for original-only (the default). It is text with an info icon, not colour only. Its tooltip/disclosure: "The search term was found in the machine translation of this article."
2. **Card headline stays in the original language** (ADR-0025 scope). For foreign articles that matched through the translation, the card also shows a one-line muted "English: <translated headline>" below the original headline so the reader can see why it matched (this uses `headline_en`; rendered as text, `lang="en"`). If there is no translated headline, the line is omitted. This single line is the only translated text on the list; cards otherwise remain original-language. UNCONFIRMED: show the English headline line for all foreign cards, not only translation matches (leaning yes, small and useful; needs the user's call, see section 12).
3. **Standing note on the search results page** (near the existing `CoverageLine`): "Search matches the original text and, where available, the English translation. N foreign-language articles in this selection are not translated yet, so English terms may miss them." Shown only when N > 0; N and the reason split appear in a disclosure ("N waiting, M paused, K failed"). The sentence is warn-styled when N is more than 5% of the selection, muted otherwise, like the existing partial-enrichment style.
4. **Empty state split** (P3): the existing "no match" message gains the same sentence when N > 0 ("No results. N foreign-language articles in this selection are not translated yet.").
5. **Search echo** (existing `echo.ts`): unchanged; it shows how the query was interpreted. A line is added when the query contains a non-Latin term: "Non-Latin terms are matched against the original text only." This explains why an Arabic term never matches a translation.
6. `NOT` semantics shown in the echo: "Excludes articles matching in the original or in the translation." (search spec decision, UNCONFIRMED).

## 7. Component specifications
| Component | Status | Purpose | Inputs | States and notes |
| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `TranslatedText` (client) | New | Holds the toggle, label bar and both text blocks | `sourceLang`, `original: {headline, body}`, `translation: {headline_en, body_en}`, `trust`, `modelInfo`, `producedAt` | `view: "translated" or "original"`; renders both blocks, hides one; live region; beacon on change |
| `TranslationNotice` (server) | New | Bar for non-translated states (pending, paused, failed, no content, not needed message) | `state`, `reason` | text only, with the explanation copy in section 9 |
| `MatchedInTag` | New, small | Search card marker | `side` (translation, both) | tooltip text; not colour-only |
| `UntranslatedNote` | New | Standing search note | `counts {queued, paused, failed}` | warn vs muted; disclosure |
| `TextBlock` | Reuse | Renders each text with `lang`, `dir="auto"`, bidi isolation | existing | unchanged; validates the BCP47 tag |
| `ArticleCard` | Reuse + small change | Adds the tag and English headline line | `matched_in`, `headline_en` | the card is a client component already |
| `CoverageLine` | Reuse | Unchanged; the new note sits next to it | | |
| `strings` (`src/lib/ui/strings`) | Reuse | Add the copy keys in section 9 | | keep copy out of components |

## 8. Key flows
1. **Read a foreign article.** Search or list, open article, read the English text, notice the "Machine translated from Arabic" label, click "Show original" to check a quote, click "Show translation" to return.
2. **Find by English term.** Type "interest rate", results include an Arabic article tagged "Matched in translation" with its English headline line, open it, default is the translation, the matching words are visible.

Base directory for this skill: C:\Users\simon\AppData\Local\Claude-Data\claude_pzs8sxrjxfjjc\local-agent-mode-sessions\skills-plugin\1cec5490-7429-4b0e-9f4f-735b92a256c6\9696b3ec-826e-4b0c-b0c0-25f9eaf3187d\skills\carma-devops

# carma-devops

The bar for this skill is simple to state and demanding to meet: on the target machine, someone runs `docker compose up` and a working, fully wired system appears. The database exists with its extensions, roles and partitions, migrations have run, the application and workers are connected, observability is collecting, and secrets are in place, all without hand-editing anything or running steps in a particular order from a README.

Read `references/carma-context.md` first for the principles, constraints and spec conventions.

Compose runs on one host. That is a real limit for a pipeline sized at 800 articles a second, so this skill checks the fit between the design and the machine honestly and says where a single host stops being enough, instead of assuming it will be.

## Inputs

Read the latest non-superseded specs for the same feature: `.specs/architect/` (components, data flow, FP and HP registers; ADRs in `.specs/architect/adrs/`), and where present `.specs/data/dba/` (extensions, config parameters, migrations, roles, capacity), `.specs/telemetry/` (collector, storage and dashboards needed), `.specs/data/sanitization/` (secrets and limits needed at runtime), `.specs/search/` (language configurations, dictionaries, extensions) and `.specs/ux/` (web app). Take from them every component that must run, every setting and secret it needs, and the throughput and capacity numbers. If the architect spec is missing, say so and ask.

Inspect the codebase for what exists: Dockerfiles, compose files, `.dockerignore`, CI configuration, environment and config files, startup and migration scripts, healthchecks, how config and secrets are read, and anything committed that looks like a secret. Record paths. Existing secrets in the repository are a finding to raise immediately.

## Workflow

### 1. Target machine and capacity fit

Establish what it runs on: operating system and architecture, CPU, memory, disk type and size, network (can it pull images, or is it offline), Docker Engine and Compose versions, and who administers it. Ask for what you cannot find. Prefer Linux for anything performance-related; Docker on a desktop OS adds a virtual machine whose I/O will mislead any benchmark.

Then test the design against the machine using the architect and DBA numbers: CPU and memory budget at 800 articles a second, database write rate, WAL and disk growth per day, the observability stack's own footprint. State clearly where one host is enough, where it is marginal, and what would break first (usually disk I/O or memory for the database). Name the point at which Compose is no longer the right tool, so the user knows it, without turning this into a platform migration plan.

### 2. Service topology

Define every service, and for each its purpose, image, ports, volumes, dependencies, resource limits and healthcheck. Typical set, to adapt to the design:

- **Database.** An image pinned by version (never `latest`), built with exactly the extensions the DBA plan needs. In Compose the image is under our control, so "is this extension permitted" is partly our choice, but record whether Carma's real environment will match, because behaviour that works here may not carry over. Tuning parameters from the DBA spec, set through configuration. Enough shared memory (`shm_size`), because the container default is small and breaks parallel queries. A named volume on fast storage for data.
- **Connection pooler** if the DBA plan includes one.
- **One-shot jobs.** Migrations, database bootstrap (roles with least privilege, extensions, initial partitions, reference data), and secret generation. These run to completion and the services that depend on them wait for that.
- **Application services.** Web app, API, ingestion workers, enrichment workers, scheduler. Workers must scale by replica count and shut down gracefully so claimed items go back to the queue (P2).
- **Edge.** A reverse proxy handling TLS if anything is exposed. Only the proxy publishes ports. The database is not published to the host by default.
- **Observability.** The collector, metric and log storage, and dashboards the telemetry spec calls for, sized so they do not starve the database.
- **Backup job** per the DBA recovery plan.
- **Optional profiles.** Compose profiles for the load generator, a disposable database for quick benchmarks (carma-benchmark runs Node.js benchmarks against it and resets it afterwards), development tools and anything not needed in normal running.

Isolate networks (an internal network for the data path, a separate edge network), run containers as non-root where the image allows, drop capabilities, use read-only filesystems where possible, and set CPU and memory limits from measured numbers rather than guesses. Pin every image, and plan how updates are chosen deliberately.

### 3. Zero-touch bring-up

This is the core requirement. Design the start sequence so it works the first time on an empty machine, again on a second run, and after a reboot.

- **Ordering by readiness, not by start.** Use healthchecks and `depends_on` with conditions (`service_healthy`, `service_completed_successfully`) so the migration job waits for a database that accepts connections and the application waits for migrations. A healthcheck must prove readiness (the database accepts a query, the worker can claim work), not that a process exists.
- **Idempotent initialisation.** Database init scripts in the standard image directory run only on an empty data directory, so anything that must apply on every start or upgrade belongs in the migration job, written to be safe to run repeatedly. Test an empty start and a restart over existing data.
- **Everything wired.** Service discovery by Compose service name, connection strings built from configuration, extensions created, roles and grants applied, partitions pre-created, reference data loaded, dashboards provisioned from files. No step is left for a human.
- **Boot survival.** Restart policies on long-running services, and the Compose project itself started at machine boot (for example a systemd unit), so a reboot recovers unattended.
- **Fast, clear failure.** If something required is missing or invalid (a secret, a setting), the stack stops with a message that says what and how to fix it, not a stack trace three services away.

### 4. Keys, secrets and configuration

Secrets are configuration with extra rules. Specify both together.

- **Inventory.** A table of every setting: name, purpose, default, required or optional, secret or not, who provides it, how it is rotated. Include database role passwords, application signing keys, LLM or scorer API keys, TLS material, and any credentials for backup storage.
- **Two kinds of secret, two mechanisms.**
  - *Internal secrets* (database role passwords, session and signing keys) can be generated. For true zero-touch, a one-shot service generates them on first run into a protected named volume that services mount read-only and read through `_FILE` style variables. (Compose's native `secrets:` with a file source expects the file to exist before `up`, so it suits provided secrets, not generated ones. Check what the installed Compose version supports, such as environment-sourced secrets.)
  - *External secrets* (an LLM provider key) cannot be generated. The user supplies them through a git-ignored file or the environment, and the stack validates their presence at start. If a required one is missing, fail with a clear message, or run in a deliberate degraded mode (for example without LLM enrichment, with confidence shown as "no confidence available", P6) if the user chooses that. Put the choice to them.
- **Rules.** No secrets in images, build arguments, the Compose file, the repository, logs or error messages; `.env` and secret files git-ignored; a committed `.env.example` with placeholders and comments; each database role has its own credential (least privilege, from the data-sanity spec); secrets reach containers as files, not command-line arguments; logs and traces redact them; the LLM key is subject to the spend limits in the data-sanity spec.
- **Rotation.** State how each secret is rotated and what restarts when it changes, and test that procedure.
- **Config layering.** Defaults in the repository, per-environment overrides through Compose override files or variables, one place per setting, validated at startup. Include the database tuning parameters from the DBA spec as versioned configuration, not edits inside a container.
- **Stronger options.** If the threat model needs more than files on a host (a secrets manager, SOPS-encrypted files, Docker Swarm secrets), list them as options with their cost, and keep the file-based design as the baseline.

### 5. Deployment, upgrade and recovery

- **Delivery.** Build images in CI and pull from a registry, or build on the target? Decide, considering whether the target has internet access. Tag releases immutably.
- **Upgrade.** The procedure to move from version N to N+1 (pull, run migrations, restart), what the data-sanity and DBA specs require for compatibility (expand then contract migrations, so the old version keeps working during the change), how workers drain, and what ingestion does during the restart: the ledger must show no articles lost (P2, P3), and anything late is flagged as late.
- **Rollback.** What can be rolled back (images, config) and what cannot (applied migrations), with the plan for each. Keep the previous images available.
- **Backup and restore.** From the DBA recovery plan: scheduled backups and WAL archiving as a Compose service, copies kept off the host, and a restore procedure that is rehearsed, not assumed.
- **Host settings that decide whether it works.** Log rotation for container logs (unbounded logs fill disks), Docker daemon settings, disk space alerts for the data volume and WAL, kernel and file-descriptor limits the database needs, and time synchronisation. The freshness target is measured from `published_at` against the machine's clock, so clock drift directly corrupts the 15-minute measurement.

### 6. Deployment test plan

A bring-up that works once on a developer's laptop proves little. Specify tests that prove the claims. The pipeline data-correctness and load tests belong to carma-backend-testing; this plan covers the deployment and the platform, and the two share the same Compose-based test environment.

- **Clean-machine bring-up.** On a fresh machine with no cached images, one command produces a healthy system within a stated time budget. This is the acceptance test for the whole skill.
- **Smoke test.** After `up`, every healthcheck is green, a few sample articles in English, Arabic and Chinese go through ingestion, appear in search, and show in telemetry, and the reconciliation count balances (the walking skeleton running as a deployment check).
- **Idempotency.** `up` twice, `down` then `up`, and reboot the machine: same healthy state, no duplicated data, no lost data.
- **Fault tests.** Kill and restart each service, stop the database mid-ingestion, fill a disk (or simulate it), hit a memory limit, and verify recovery and that the failure is visible in telemetry and in the reconciliation counts.
- **Upgrade and rollback.** Upgrade from the previous version with real data in place, and roll back what can be rolled back.
- **Backup and restore.** Restore into a clean environment and verify counts and content hashes against the source.
- **Secrets and exposure.** Missing or malformed secrets give clear failures; no secrets in image layers, environment dumps, `docker inspect`, logs or the repository (use secret scanning and image scanning); only intended ports are reachable from outside; the database is not exposed.
- **Config validation.** Bad values are rejected at startup with a useful message.
- **Capacity check.** Run the load profile from the testing spec on the target hardware and compare the results with the capacity fit from step 1.
- **CI.** Validate the Compose files, scan images and secrets, bring the stack up in CI, and run the smoke and integration tests against it on every change.

### 7. Failure points and hot paths

Extend the architect registers with `FP-V` and `HP-V` entries in the same format. Typical candidates: the single host as a single point of failure, disk full from data, WAL or logs, out-of-memory kills, a startup race when a healthcheck lies, init scripts that only run once, secret rotation breaking connections, image tag drift between environments, clock drift, port conflicts, and the observability stack competing with the database for resources.

### 8. Decisions to put to the user

Raise choices that need a human: the target hardware and whether one host is acceptable as the long-term target, building on the target or pulling from a registry, auto-generated versus provided secrets and what happens when an external key is missing, whether the observability stack is on by default or a profile, TLS and domain, backup destination and recovery targets. Use the protocol in the context file.

## Output

Write the spec with these sections:

1. **Summary** (what comes up from one command, and whether one host is enough)
2. **Inputs and current state** (existing Docker and CI files with paths, secrets findings)
3. **Target machine and capacity fit**
4. **Service topology** (table: service, purpose, image, ports, volumes, depends on, healthcheck, resource limits; network diagram; an illustrative Compose sketch labelled as such)
5. **Zero-touch bring-up sequence** (ordered steps with the readiness gate for each)
6. **Configuration and secrets** (inventory table, generation and supply mechanisms, rules, rotation)
7. **Deployment, upgrade, rollback and recovery**
8. **Host and platform settings**
9. **Deployment test plan** (table: test, what it proves, how, pass criteria)
10. **Repository artefacts to create** (Compose files, Dockerfiles, `.env.example`, bootstrap and migration jobs, CI configuration, documentation)
11. **Risks and hot paths** (`FP-V` and `HP-V`)
12. **Handoff** (to carma-backend-testing for the shared test environment, and to carma-plan for tasks)
13. **Decisions needed and open questions**

# Production hardening: pin image digests (repo@sha256:…) once verified in your registry.

x-logging: &logging
  driver: json-file
  options: { max-size: "10m", max-file: "3" }

x-app: &app
  image: media-signal-app:local
  build: { context: ., target: runner }
  init: true
  read_only: true
  cap_drop: [ALL]

services:

        volume:

    shm_size: 256mb
    mem_limit: 1g
    healthcheck:
      test: ["CMD-SHELL", "pg_isready -h 127.0.0.1 -U mss_admin -d $${POSTGRES_DB}"]
      interval: 5s
      timeout: 3s
      retries: 20
      start_period: 10s
    restart: unless-stopped
    networks: [data]
    logging: *logging

  migrate:
    <<: *app
    command: ["node", "dist/cli/migrate.js"]
    environment:
      ROLE: migrate
      DB_HOST: db
      DB_PORT: "5432"
      DB_NAME: ${DB_NAME:-mss}

      ENRICHMENT_ENABLED: ${ENRICHMENT_ENABLED:-true}
      SEED_SAMPLE: ${SEED_SAMPLE:-true}
      PROMPT_VERSION: ${PROMPT_VERSION:-v1}
      MIGRATIONS_DIR: /app/db/migrations
    volumes:
      - type: volume
        source: secrets
        target: /run/secrets
        read_only: true
        volume:
          subpath: migrate
    depends_on:
      db:
        condition: service_healthy
      secrets-init:
        condition: service_completed_successfully
    restart: "no"
    networks: [data]
    mem_limit: 256m

  # Optional re-seed / extra loads (sample is also loaded by migrate when SEED_SAMPLE=true)
  seed:
    <<: *app
    profiles: [seed]
    command: ["node", "dist/cli/load.js", "--file", "/app/data/sample_articles.json", "--kind", "backfill"]
    environment:
      ROLE: seed
      DB_HOST: db
      DB_PORT: "5432"
      DB_NAME: ${DB_NAME:-mss}
      DB_PASSWORD_FILE: /run/secrets/app_ingest_password
      SEED_SAMPLE: ${SEED_SAMPLE:-true}
      PROMPT_VERSION: ${PROMPT_VERSION:-v1}
    volumes:
      - type: volume
        source: secrets
        target: /run/secrets
        read_only: true
        volume:
          subpath: seed
    depends_on:
      migrate:
        condition: service_completed_successfully
    restart: "no"
    networks: [data]
    mem_limit: 256m

  web:
    <<: *app
    command: ["node", "server.js"]
    environment:
      ROLE: web
      DB_HOST: db
      DB_PORT: "5432"
      DB_NAME: ${DB_NAME:-mss}
      DB_PASSWORD_FILE: /run/secrets/app_read_password
      CURSOR_SECRET_FILE: /run/secrets/cursor_secret
      INGEST_DB_PASSWORD_FILE: /run/secrets/app_ingest_password
      UPLOAD_TOKEN_FILE: /run/secrets/upload_token
      UPLOAD_ENABLED: ${UPLOAD_ENABLED:-true}
      UPLOAD_MAX_BYTES: ${UPLOAD_MAX_BYTES:-5242880}
      UPLOAD_MAX_ITEMS: ${UPLOAD_MAX_ITEMS:-1000}
      INGEST_STATEMENT_TIMEOUT_MS: ${INGEST_STATEMENT_TIMEOUT_MS:-10000}
      UPLOAD_DEADLINE_MS: ${UPLOAD_DEADLINE_MS:-60000}
      HOSTNAME: 0.0.0.0
      PORT: "3000"
    ports:
      - "${WEB_BIND:-127.0.0.1}:${WEB_PORT:-3000}:3000"
    networks: [data, edge]
    tmpfs:
      - /tmp:size=64m
      - /app/.next/cache
    volumes:
      - type: volume
        source: secrets
        target: /run/secrets
# Optional. Copy to .env for local overrides. Internal secrets are generated by Compose.

WEB_BIND=127.0.0.1
DB_NAME=mss
DB_TUNING=small
DB_HOST=db

# ADR-0013: Fall back to a labelled mock adapter when a provider key is missing

## Context and problem statement
Graders may run the stack without keys. The user will supply keys for real runs. Devops DV1.

## Considered options
1. `ENRICHMENT_MODE=auto`: each provider independently uses the mock when its key is absent (recommended)
2. Fail fast without both keys

## Decision outcome
Chosen option 1. Mock values carry origin `mock` and the UI shows 'Mock output'. `real` mode remains available and fails fast on a missing key.

### Consequences
- Good: runs anywhere; tests use the same path.
- Bad: someone may mistake mock output for real; mitigated by origin labelling (FP-17, FP-D15).

# ADR-0013: Fall back to a labelled mock adapter when a provider key is missing

## Context and problem statement
Graders may run the stack without keys. The user will supply keys for real runs. Devops DV1.

## Considered options
1. `ENRICHMENT_MODE=auto`: each provider independently uses the mock when its key is absent (recommended)
2. Fail fast without both keys

## Decision outcome
Chosen option 1. Mock values carry origin `mock` and the UI shows 'Mock output'. `real` mode remains available and fails fast on a missing key.

### Consequences
- Good: runs anywhere; tests use the same path.
- Bad: someone may mistake mock output for real; mitigated by origin labelling (FP-17, FP-D15).

# 0003 Deployment delta for article translation

## 1. Summary
No new service, image or secret. `docker compose up` on an existing install rebuilds the app image, the `migrate` job applies `0004_article_translations.sql`, the worker starts a translation lane, and Prometheus/Grafana pick up new alert and dashboard files. New settings are plain configuration with safe defaults. The translation lane reuses the existing `OPENAI_API_KEY`; without a key it runs a clearly labelled mock translator (ADR-0013). One host is enough for the PoC volume; at the 800/s design target translating every foreign article is not feasible on one host or within a sensible LLM budget (section 3), which is the main finding.

## 2. Inputs and current state
- `compose.yaml`: `secrets-init`, `db` (postgres 16.6, `mem_limit 1g`), `migrate` (one-shot, `service_completed_successfully` gate), `seed` (profile), `web`, plus worker, Prometheus and Grafana further down. App services share the `x-app` anchor: `read_only`, `cap_drop: ALL`, `no-new-privileges`, `.env` optional.
- `.env.example` already carries the provider, budget and worker settings: `OPENAI_API_KEY`, `OPENAI_MODEL`, `BUDGET_OPENAI_DAILY=10`, `WORKER_CONCURRENCY_OPENAI=2`, `RPM_OPENAI=60`, `MAX_ATTEMPTS=4`, `CALL_TIMEOUT_MS=30000`, `INPUT_TOKEN_CAP=4000`, `ENRICHMENT_MODE=auto`. Settings are validated by a zod schema in `src/lib/config.ts` (lines 40 to 75, mapped around 255 to 275).
- Migrations run from `MIGRATIONS_DIR=/app/db/migrations` in `migrate`; roles and passwords are managed there (`set_role_password`).
- Observability: `ops/prometheus.yml`, `ops/alerts.yml`, `ops/grafana/provisioning` (devops 0002 added U1 to U5).
- No secrets found in the repository for this feature. `OPENAI_API_KEY` is read from `.env` / environment for the worker, never committed (`.env.example` has it commented out).
- Finding (worker, `src/worker/loop.ts`): the claim cycle holds one pooled connection (`client`) until the end of the `finally`, i.e. across the provider calls of every claimed job, even though the claim transaction is already committed. With translation jobs lasting up to minutes (up to 20 chunks), a held connection per lane would waste connections. Release the client right after `COMMIT` (it is not used afterwards). This is part of the plan.

## 3. Target machine and capacity fit
Target machine: unknown (CPU, memory, disk, OS), UNCONFIRMED (same as devops 0001/0002).

Translation is LLM-bound, not host-bound. Assume `B` = 3 KB body, about 750 input tokens in English or about 1,000 in Arabic, similar output, so about 1.5 to 2k tokens per article, about 2 provider calls per article (1,500-token chunks).
| Scenario | Foreign articles/day | Calls/s | Tokens/day | Fit |
| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
| PoC (50,000/day, f = 30%) | 15,000 | 0.35 | about 25 to 30 M | Fits: `RPM_OPENAI`-style limit of 60/min is enough; set the translate lane to 2 workers |
| Design target, f = 10% (800/s) | 6.9 M | about 160 | about 10 to 14 B | Does not fit: far above any default rate limit and any plausible daily budget |
| Design target, f = 30% | 20.7 M | about 480 | about 30 to 40 B | Does not fit |
Postgres load is small by comparison (DBA 0003 section 3). What breaks first at the design target is the provider's rate limit and the budget, not CPU, memory or disk. With ADR-0010 deferral the queue would grow without bound and most foreign articles would sit in `deferred_budget` for days. Consequence for the plan: ADR-0022 (translate everything at ingest) is right for the PoC and should be revisited as hybrid (translate on demand and for recent or prioritised articles, ADR-0022 option 3) before any move toward the 800/s target. Recorded as a risk (FP-V1), not changed here.

Host additions: worker memory rises slightly (chunk buffers; keep `mem_limit` at the current value and re-measure), CPU is negligible (validators are linear text scans). Disk growth for translations is in DBA 0003 (about 75 MB/day at PoC volume).

## 4. Service topology (delta)
| Service | Change |
| --- | --- |
| `db` | No image or extension change. Disk: see DBA 0003. `shm_size` unchanged |
| `migrate` | Applies `0004`. The constraint changes use `NOT VALID` then `VALIDATE` (DBA 0003 section 10), so the one-shot job stays short on large job tables |
| `worker` | Image rebuilt. New translation lane with its own concurrency, rate limit, breaker name `openai-translate` and budget. Env: new variables in section 6. Needs the same `OPENAI_API_KEY` file/env as today. Graceful shutdown: on SIGTERM it stops claiming and lets in-flight chunk calls finish or release the claim (visibility timeout covers a hard kill) |
| `web` | Image rebuilt (article page, search, `POST /api/telemetry/translation-view`). No new secret. Needs read access to `article_translations` through the existing `app_read` role |
| `prometheus`, `grafana` | Mount updated `ops/alerts.yml` (T1 to T8) and a new dashboard JSON row. No new container |
| `secrets-init` | No change |
There is no network or port change. The beacon route is served by `web` on the existing port.

## 5. Zero-touch bring-up sequence
Same as today; the new steps are inside existing gates.
1. `secrets-init` (unchanged) then `db` healthy.
2. `migrate` runs migrations in order, including `0004`; it is idempotent (`IF NOT EXISTS`, constraint swap guarded by catalog lookups) and writes `system_flags` `translation_enabled` (from `TRANSLATION_ENABLED`, default true) next to `enrichment_enabled`.
3. `worker` and `web` start only after `migrate` completes; `web` readiness (`/api/health`) additionally checks that `article_translations` exists, so a code/schema mismatch fails readiness instead of failing on first article view.
4. Worker readiness: it can claim a job of each part; the translation lane starts in "mock" or "real" mode and logs which, once, at startup (`translation.provider_mode`), and exposes it in `/api/status`.
5. Prometheus loads rules; Grafana provisions the dashboard. If a rules file is invalid, Prometheus exits with a clear message (checked in CI with `promtool check rules`).
Validation at startup (zod): an out-of-range value stops the process with the variable name and the allowed range.

## 6. Configuration and secrets
No new secrets. `OPENAI_API_KEY` is the existing external secret (supplied via `.env`; failure behaviour as ADR-0013).
| Name | Purpose | Default | Secret | Provided by | Rotation / restart |
| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `TRANSLATION_ENABLED` | Seed value of the `translation_enabled` flag; the flag itself is the live kill switch | `true` | No | `.env`, then flag via SQL | flag is read each loop, no restart; flip with `UPDATE system_flags` |
| `TRANSLATE_MODEL` | Model id for translation | falls back to `OPENAI_MODEL` | No | `.env` | restart worker; recorded per row (P7) |
| `WORKER_CONCURRENCY_TRANSLATE` | In-flight translation jobs | `2` | No | `.env` | restart worker |
| `RPM_TRANSLATE` | Request cap for the lane | `60` | No | `.env` | restart worker |
| `BUDGET_TRANSLATE_DAILY` | Daily cap for translation, in `BUDGET_CURRENCY` (separate ledger key `openai-translate`; proposed 30% of the OpenAI cap) | `3` | No | `.env` | restart worker |
| `TRANSLATE_CHUNK_TOKENS` | Estimated tokens per chunk | `1500` | No | `.env` | restart worker; changes `prompt_version` suffix so cache keys differ |
| `TRANSLATE_MAX_CHUNKS` | Hard cap per article; beyond it the job is dead `too_long` | `20` | No | `.env` | restart worker |
| `TRANSLATE_RATIO_CJK`, `TRANSLATE_RATIO_OTHER` | Output/input length bounds, "min,max" | `0.15,4.0` and `0.3,3.0` | No | `.env` | restart worker |
| `TRANSLATE_CACHE_DAYS` | Chunk cache retention after job end | `7` | No | `.env` | sweeper reads each run |
| `TRANSLATE_SUPERSEDED_DAYS` | Retention of superseded translations | `30` | No | `.env` | sweeper reads each run |
| `TRANSLATE_PROMPT_VERSION` | Prompt id, recorded on every row | `t1` | No | `.env` | restart worker |
Provider prices reuse `OPENAI_PRICE_IN_PER_MTOK` and `OPENAI_PRICE_OUT_PER_MTOK`. When prices are unset the existing behaviour applies (estimated cost flagged; budget placeholder), unchanged.
Rules kept: no setting is baked into an image; `.env.example` gets the lines above commented with defaults; values are validated in `src/lib/config.ts`; the translation text and the key never appear in logs (telemetry 0003 section 5).

### Mock translator (no key, ADR-0013)
- `ENRICHMENT_MODE=auto` with no `OPENAI_API_KEY`: the translation lane uses the mock. In `real` mode a missing key fails fast at startup, as for the other parts.
- The mock must not pass as a real translation. Rows get `enrichments.origin = 'mock'`, `provider = 'mock'`; the output starts each paragraph with `[mock translation]` followed by deterministic Latin placeholder words of about the source length, so it differs from the input, passes the language, echo and ratio checks, and keeps the paragraph count. For the bundled sample articles a small fixture lexicon (same idea as the existing mock adapter, `src/lib/providers/mock.ts`) supplies readable English so graders can see the feature.
- UI: origin `mock` replaces the bar label with "Mock translation (no translation service configured)", and the "About this" panel says no external call was made. Search treats it like any translation, so it is searchable, but `matched_in` markers say "Matched in translation (mock)".
- Mock latency uses `MOCK_LATENCY_MS`; no budget is consumed (cost 0, `origin` mock), so grader runs never hit `deferred_budget`.

## 7. Deployment, upgrade, rollback and recovery
Upgrade from the current release (with data):
1. `git pull`, `docker compose build`.
2. `docker compose up -d`: `migrate` runs `0004`; `web` and `worker` restart on the new image. Ingestion through the web upload route pauses for the few seconds of the web restart; the upload endpoint is idempotent (devops 0002) and reconciliation shows no loss.
3. Existing foreign articles have no translation job. Backfill is optional and off by default (DBA 0003 section 10): a one-line SQL or a `--backfill-translations` option on the CLI queues jobs in batches of 1,000, paced by the budget. UNCONFIRMED whether the user wants it.
4. Verify: `/api/status` shows `translation` counts; open a foreign article; the dashboard row shows jobs moving.
Rollback:
- Fast stop without code change: `UPDATE system_flags SET value='false' WHERE key='translation_enabled'` (worker stops claiming; existing translations still display).
- Code rollback: redeploy the previous image. The old code ignores `translation` jobs, but the old worker's `claimJobs` filters by part, so they stay queued harmlessly; the new `ingest_new_version` signature breaks the old web image (it calls the old signature), so roll back web and worker together and run the DBA rollback script if the old signature must come back (DBA 0003 section 10).
- Data rollback: DBA rollback section; originals are untouched, so nothing is lost.
Backup/restore: `article_translations` is in the normal database backup; no extra step. Restore test checks translation counts and that the current-row unique index holds. Translations are re-creatable but cost money, so they are not excluded from backups.
