# 0003 Deployment delta for article translation

## 1. Summary
No new service, image or secret. `docker compose up` on an existing install rebuilds the app image, the `migrate` job applies `0004_article_translations.sql`, the worker starts a translation lane, and Prometheus/Grafana pick up new alert and dashboard files. New settings are plain configuration with safe defaults. The translation lane reuses the existing `OPENAI_API_KEY`; without a key it runs a clearly labelled mock translator (ADR-0013). One host is enough for the PoC volume; at the 800/s design target translating every foreign article is not feasible on one host or within a sensible LLM budget (section 3), which is the main finding.

## 2. Inputs and current state
- `compose.yaml`: `secrets-init`, `db` (postgres 16.6, `mem_limit 1g`), `migrate` (one-shot, `service_completed_successfully` gate), `seed` (profile), `web`, plus worker, Prometheus and Grafana further down. App services share the `x-app` anchor: `read_only`, `cap_drop: ALL`, `no-new-privileges`, `.env` optional.
- `.env.example` already carries the provider, budget and worker settings: `OPENAI_API_KEY`, `OPENAI_MODEL`, `BUDGET_OPENAI_DAILY=10`, `WORKER_CONCURRENCY_OPENAI=2`, `RPM_OPENAI=60`, `MAX_ATTEMPTS=4`, `CALL_TIMEOUT_MS=30000`, `INPUT_TOKEN_CAP=4000`, `ENRICHMENT_MODE=auto`. Settings are validated by a zod schema in `src/lib/config.ts` (lines 40 to 75, mapped around 255 to 275).
- Migrations run from `MIGRATIONS_DIR=/app/db/migrations` in `migrate`; roles and passwords are managed there (`set_role_password`).
- Observability: `ops/prometheus.yml`, `ops/alerts.yml`, `ops/grafana/provisioning` (devops 0002 added U1 to U5).
- No secrets found in the repository for this feature. `OPENAI_API_KEY` is read from `.env` / environment for the worker, never committed (`.env.example` has it commented out).
- Finding (worker, `src/worker/loop.ts`): the claim cycle holds one pooled connection (`client`) until the end of the `finally`, i.e. across the provider calls of every claimed job, even though the claim transaction is already committed. With translation jobs lasting up to minutes (up to 20 chunks), a held connection per lane would waste connections. Release the client right after `COMMIT` (it is not used afterwards). This is part of the plan.

## 3. Target machine and capacity fit
Target machine: unknown (CPU, memory, disk, OS), UNCONFIRMED (same as devops 0001/0002).

Translation is LLM-bound, not host-bound. Assume `B` = 3 KB body, about 750 input tokens in English or about 1,000 in Arabic, similar output, so about 1.5 to 2k tokens per article, about 2 provider calls per article (1,500-token chunks).
| Scenario | Foreign articles/day | Calls/s | Tokens/day | Fit |
| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
| PoC (50,000/day, f = 30%) | 15,000 | 0.35 | about 25 to 30 M | Fits: `RPM_OPENAI`-style limit of 60/min is enough; set the translate lane to 2 workers |
| Design target, f = 10% (800/s) | 6.9 M | about 160 | about 10 to 14 B | Does not fit: far above any default rate limit and any plausible daily budget |
| Design target, f = 30% | 20.7 M | about 480 | about 30 to 40 B | Does not fit |
Postgres load is small by comparison (DBA 0003 section 3). What breaks first at the design target is the provider's rate limit and the budget, not CPU, memory or disk. With ADR-0010 deferral the queue would grow without bound and most foreign articles would sit in `deferred_budget` for days. Consequence for the plan: ADR-0022 (translate everything at ingest) is right for the PoC and should be revisited as hybrid (translate on demand and for recent or prioritised articles, ADR-0022 option 3) before any move toward the 800/s target. Recorded as a risk (FP-V1), not changed here.

Host additions: worker memory rises slightly (chunk buffers; keep `mem_limit` at the current value and re-measure), CPU is negligible (validators are linear text scans). Disk growth for translations is in DBA 0003 (about 75 MB/day at PoC volume).

## 4. Service topology (delta)
| Service | Change |
| --- | --- |
| `db` | No image or extension change. Disk: see DBA 0003. `shm_size` unchanged |
| `migrate` | Applies `0004`. The constraint changes use `NOT VALID` then `VALIDATE` (DBA 0003 section 10), so the one-shot job stays short on large job tables |
| `worker` | Image rebuilt. New translation lane with its own concurrency, rate limit, breaker name `openai-translate` and budget. Env: new variables in section 6. Needs the same `OPENAI_API_KEY` file/env as today. Graceful shutdown: on SIGTERM it stops claiming and lets in-flight chunk calls finish or release the claim (visibility timeout covers a hard kill) |
| `web` | Image rebuilt (article page, search, `POST /api/telemetry/translation-view`). No new secret. Needs read access to `article_translations` through the existing `app_read` role |
| `prometheus`, `grafana` | Mount updated `ops/alerts.yml` (T1 to T8) and a new dashboard JSON row. No new container |
| `secrets-init` | No change |
There is no network or port change. The beacon route is served by `web` on the existing port.

## 5. Zero-touch bring-up sequence
Same as today; the new steps are inside existing gates.
1. `secrets-init` (unchanged) then `db` healthy.
2. `migrate` runs migrations in order, including `0004`; it is idempotent (`IF NOT EXISTS`, constraint swap guarded by catalog lookups) and writes `system_flags` `translation_enabled` (from `TRANSLATION_ENABLED`, default true) next to `enrichment_enabled`.
3. `worker` and `web` start only after `migrate` completes; `web` readiness (`/api/health`) additionally checks that `article_translations` exists, so a code/schema mismatch fails readiness instead of failing on first article view.
4. Worker readiness: it can claim a job of each part; the translation lane starts in "mock" or "real" mode and logs which, once, at startup (`translation.provider_mode`), and exposes it in `/api/status`.
5. Prometheus loads rules; Grafana provisions the dashboard. If a rules file is invalid, Prometheus exits with a clear message (checked in CI with `promtool check rules`).
Validation at startup (zod): an out-of-range value stops the process with the variable name and the allowed range.

## 6. Configuration and secrets
No new secrets. `OPENAI_API_KEY` is the existing external secret (supplied via `.env`; failure behaviour as ADR-0013).
| Name | Purpose | Default | Secret | Provided by | Rotation / restart |
| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `TRANSLATION_ENABLED` | Seed value of the `translation_enabled` flag; the flag itself is the live kill switch | `true` | No | `.env`, then flag via SQL | flag is read each loop, no restart; flip with `UPDATE system_flags` |
| `TRANSLATE_MODEL` | Model id for translation | falls back to `OPENAI_MODEL` | No | `.env` | restart worker; recorded per row (P7) |
| `WORKER_CONCURRENCY_TRANSLATE` | In-flight translation jobs | `2` | No | `.env` | restart worker |
| `RPM_TRANSLATE` | Request cap for the lane | `60` | No | `.env` | restart worker |
| `BUDGET_TRANSLATE_DAILY` | Daily cap for translation, in `BUDGET_CURRENCY` (separate ledger key `openai-translate`; proposed 30% of the OpenAI cap) | `3` | No | `.env` | restart worker |
| `TRANSLATE_CHUNK_TOKENS` | Estimated tokens per chunk | `1500` | No | `.env` | restart worker; changes `prompt_version` suffix so cache keys differ |
| `TRANSLATE_MAX_CHUNKS` | Hard cap per article; beyond it the job is dead `too_long` | `20` | No | `.env` | restart worker |
| `TRANSLATE_RATIO_CJK`, `TRANSLATE_RATIO_OTHER` | Output/input length bounds, "min,max" | `0.15,4.0` and `0.3,3.0` | No | `.env` | restart worker |
| `TRANSLATE_CACHE_DAYS` | Chunk cache retention after job end | `7` | No | `.env` | sweeper reads each run |
| `TRANSLATE_SUPERSEDED_DAYS` | Retention of superseded translations | `30` | No | `.env` | sweeper reads each run |
| `TRANSLATE_PROMPT_VERSION` | Prompt id, recorded on every row | `t1` | No | `.env` | restart worker |
Provider prices reuse `OPENAI_PRICE_IN_PER_MTOK` and `OPENAI_PRICE_OUT_PER_MTOK`. When prices are unset the existing behaviour applies (estimated cost flagged; budget placeholder), unchanged.
Rules kept: no setting is baked into an image; `.env.example` gets the lines above commented with defaults; values are validated in `src/lib/config.ts`; the translation text and the key never appear in logs (telemetry 0003 section 5).

### Mock translator (no key, ADR-0013)
- `ENRICHMENT_MODE=auto` with no `OPENAI_API_KEY`: the translation lane uses the mock. In `real` mode a missing key fails fast at startup, as for the other parts.
- The mock must not pass as a real translation. Rows get `enrichments.origin = 'mock'`, `provider = 'mock'`; the output starts each paragraph with `[mock translation]` followed by deterministic Latin placeholder words of about the source length, so it differs from the input, passes the language, echo and ratio checks, and keeps the paragraph count. For the bundled sample articles a small fixture lexicon (same idea as the existing mock adapter, `src/lib/providers/mock.ts`) supplies readable English so graders can see the feature.
- UI: origin `mock` replaces the bar label with "Mock translation (no translation service configured)", and the "About this" panel says no external call was made. Search treats it like any translation, so it is searchable, but `matched_in` markers say "Matched in translation (mock)".
- Mock latency uses `MOCK_LATENCY_MS`; no budget is consumed (cost 0, `origin` mock), so grader runs never hit `deferred_budget`.

## 7. Deployment, upgrade, rollback and recovery
Upgrade from the current release (with data):
1. `git pull`, `docker compose build`.
2. `docker compose up -d`: `migrate` runs `0004`; `web` and `worker` restart on the new image. Ingestion through the web upload route pauses for the few seconds of the web restart; the upload endpoint is idempotent (devops 0002) and reconciliation shows no loss.
3. Existing foreign articles have no translation job. Backfill is optional and off by default (DBA 0003 section 10): a one-line SQL or a `--backfill-translations` option on the CLI queues jobs in batches of 1,000, paced by the budget. UNCONFIRMED whether the user wants it.
4. Verify: `/api/status` shows `translation` counts; open a foreign article; the dashboard row shows jobs moving.
Rollback:
- Fast stop without code change: `UPDATE system_flags SET value='false' WHERE key='translation_enabled'` (worker stops claiming; existing translations still display).
- Code rollback: redeploy the previous image. The old code ignores `translation` jobs, but the old worker's `claimJobs` filters by part, so they stay queued harmlessly; the new `ingest_new_version` signature breaks the old web image (it calls the old signature), so roll back web and worker together and run the DBA rollback script if the old signature must come back (DBA 0003 section 10).
- Data rollback: DBA rollback section; originals are untouched, so nothing is lost.
Backup/restore: `article_translations` is in the normal database backup; no extra step. Restore test checks translation counts and that the current-row unique index holds. Translations are re-creatable but cost money, so they are not excluded from backups.

Set the worker pool max to at least `jev + openai + translate` concurrency plus 2; check the current value in `src/lib/db/pool.ts` before changing (UNCONFIRMED).

# 0003 Deployment delta for article translation

## 1. Summary
No new service, image or secret. `docker compose up` on an existing install rebuilds the app image, the `migrate` job applies `0004_article_translations.sql`, the worker starts a translation lane, and Prometheus/Grafana pick up new alert and dashboard files. New settings are plain configuration with safe defaults. The translation lane reuses the existing `OPENAI_API_KEY`; without a key it runs a clearly labelled mock translator (ADR-0013). One host is enough for the PoC volume; at the 800/s design target translating every foreign article is not feasible on one host or within a sensible LLM budget (section 3), which is the main finding.

## 2. Inputs and current state
- `compose.yaml`: `secrets-init`, `db` (postgres 16.6, `mem_limit 1g`), `migrate` (one-shot, `service_completed_successfully` gate), `seed` (profile), `web`, plus worker, Prometheus and Grafana further down. App services share the `x-app` anchor: `read_only`, `cap_drop: ALL`, `no-new-privileges`, `.env` optional.
- `.env.example` already carries the provider, budget and worker settings: `OPENAI_API_KEY`, `OPENAI_MODEL`, `BUDGET_OPENAI_DAILY=10`, `WORKER_CONCURRENCY_OPENAI=2`, `RPM_OPENAI=60`, `MAX_ATTEMPTS=4`, `CALL_TIMEOUT_MS=30000`, `INPUT_TOKEN_CAP=4000`, `ENRICHMENT_MODE=auto`. Settings are validated by a zod schema in `src/lib/config.ts` (lines 40 to 75, mapped around 255 to 275).
- Migrations run from `MIGRATIONS_DIR=/app/db/migrations` in `migrate`; roles and passwords are managed there (`set_role_password`).
- Observability: `ops/prometheus.yml`, `ops/alerts.yml`, `ops/grafana/provisioning` (devops 0002 added U1 to U5).
- No secrets found in the repository for this feature. `OPENAI_API_KEY` is read from `.env` / environment for the worker, never committed (`.env.example` has it commented out).
- Finding (worker, `src/worker/loop.ts`): the claim cycle holds one pooled connection (`client`) until the end of the `finally`, i.e. across the provider calls of every claimed job, even though the claim transaction is already committed. With translation jobs lasting up to minutes (up to 20 chunks), a held connection per lane would waste connections. Release the client right after `COMMIT` (it is not used afterwards). This is part of the plan.

## 3. Target machine and capacity fit
Target machine: unknown (CPU, memory, disk, OS), UNCONFIRMED (same as devops 0001/0002).

Translation is LLM-bound, not host-bound. Assume `B` = 3 KB body, about 750 input tokens in English or about 1,000 in Arabic, similar output, so about 1.5 to 2k tokens per article, about 2 provider calls per article (1,500-token chunks).
| Scenario | Foreign articles/day | Calls/s | Tokens/day | Fit |
| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
| PoC (50,000/day, f = 30%) | 15,000 | 0.35 | about 25 to 30 M | Fits: `RPM_OPENAI`-style limit of 60/min is enough; set the translate lane to 2 workers |
| Design target, f = 10% (800/s) | 6.9 M | about 160 | about 10 to 14 B | Does not fit: far above any default rate limit and any plausible daily budget |
| Design target, f = 30% | 20.7 M | about 480 | about 30 to 40 B | Does not fit |
Postgres load is small by comparison (DBA 0003 section 3). What breaks first at the design target is the provider's rate limit and the budget, not CPU, memory or disk. With ADR-0010 deferral the queue would grow without bound and most foreign articles would sit in `deferred_budget` for days. Consequence for the plan: ADR-0022 (translate everything at ingest) is right for the PoC and should be revisited as hybrid (translate on demand and for recent or prioritised articles, ADR-0022 option 3) before any move toward the 800/s target. Recorded as a risk (FP-V1), not changed here.

Host additions: worker memory rises slightly (chunk buffers; keep `mem_limit` at the current value and re-measure), CPU is negligible (validators are linear text scans). Disk growth for translations is in DBA 0003 (about 75 MB/day at PoC volume).

## 4. Service topology (delta)
| Service | Change |
| --- | --- |
| `db` | No image or extension change. Disk: see DBA 0003. `shm_size` unchanged |
| `migrate` | Applies `0004`. The constraint changes use `NOT VALID` then `VALIDATE` (DBA 0003 section 10), so the one-shot job stays short on large job tables |
| `worker` | Image rebuilt. New translation lane with its own concurrency, rate limit, breaker name `openai-translate` and budget. Env: new variables in section 6. Needs the same `OPENAI_API_KEY` file/env as today. Graceful shutdown: on SIGTERM it stops claiming and lets in-flight chunk calls finish or release the claim (visibility timeout covers a hard kill) |
| `web` | Image rebuilt (article page, search, `POST /api/telemetry/translation-view`). No new secret. Needs read access to `article_translations` through the existing `app_read` role |
| `prometheus`, `grafana` | Mount updated `ops/alerts.yml` (T1 to T8) and a new dashboard JSON row. No new container |
| `secrets-init` | No change |
There is no network or port change. The beacon route is served by `web` on the existing port.

## 5. Zero-touch bring-up sequence
Same as today; the new steps are inside existing gates.
1. `secrets-init` (unchanged) then `db` healthy.
2. `migrate` runs migrations in order, including `0004`; it is idempotent (`IF NOT EXISTS`, constraint swap guarded by catalog lookups) and writes `system_flags` `translation_enabled` (from `TRANSLATION_ENABLED`, default true) next to `enrichment_enabled`.
3. `worker` and `web` start only after `migrate` completes; `web` readiness (`/api/health`) additionally checks that `article_translations` exists, so a code/schema mismatch fails readiness instead of failing on first article view.
4. Worker readiness: it can claim a job of each part; the translation lane starts in "mock" or "real" mode and logs which, once, at startup (`translation.provider_mode`), and exposes it in `/api/status`.
5. Prometheus loads rules; Grafana provisions the dashboard. If a rules file is invalid, Prometheus exits with a clear message (checked in CI with `promtool check rules`).
Validation at startup (zod): an out-of-range value stops the process with the variable name and the allowed range.

## 6. Configuration and secrets
No new secrets. `OPENAI_API_KEY` is the existing external secret (supplied via `.env`; failure behaviour as ADR-0013).
| Name | Purpose | Default | Secret | Provided by | Rotation / restart |
| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `TRANSLATION_ENABLED` | Seed value of the `translation_enabled` flag; the flag itself is the live kill switch | `true` | No | `.env`, then flag via SQL | flag is read each loop, no restart; flip with `UPDATE system_flags` |
| `TRANSLATE_MODEL` | Model id for translation | falls back to `OPENAI_MODEL` | No | `.env` | restart worker; recorded per row (P7) |
| `WORKER_CONCURRENCY_TRANSLATE` | In-flight translation jobs | `2` | No | `.env` | restart worker |
| `RPM_TRANSLATE` | Request cap for the lane | `60` | No | `.env` | restart worker |
| `BUDGET_TRANSLATE_DAILY` | Daily cap for translation, in `BUDGET_CURRENCY` (separate ledger key `openai-translate`; proposed 30% of the OpenAI cap) | `3` | No | `.env` | restart worker |
| `TRANSLATE_CHUNK_TOKENS` | Estimated tokens per chunk | `1500` | No | `.env` | restart worker; changes `prompt_version` suffix so cache keys differ |
| `TRANSLATE_MAX_CHUNKS` | Hard cap per article; beyond it the job is dead `too_long` | `20` | No | `.env` | restart worker |
| `TRANSLATE_RATIO_CJK`, `TRANSLATE_RATIO_OTHER` | Output/input length bounds, "min,max" | `0.15,4.0` and `0.3,3.0` | No | `.env` | restart worker |
| `TRANSLATE_CACHE_DAYS` | Chunk cache retention after job end | `7` | No | `.env` | sweeper reads each run |
| `TRANSLATE_SUPERSEDED_DAYS` | Retention of superseded translations | `30` | No | `.env` | sweeper reads each run |
| `TRANSLATE_PROMPT_VERSION` | Prompt id, recorded on every row | `t1` | No | `.env` | restart worker |
Provider prices reuse `OPENAI_PRICE_IN_PER_MTOK` and `OPENAI_PRICE_OUT_PER_MTOK`. When prices are unset the existing behaviour applies (estimated cost flagged; budget placeholder), unchanged.
Rules kept: no setting is baked into an image; `.env.example` gets the lines above commented with defaults; values are validated in `src/lib/config.ts`; the translation text and the key never appear in logs (telemetry 0003 section 5).

### Mock translator (no key, ADR-0013)
- `ENRICHMENT_MODE=auto` with no `OPENAI_API_KEY`: the translation lane uses the mock. In `real` mode a missing key fails fast at startup, as for the other parts.
- The mock must not pass as a real translation. Rows get `enrichments.origin = 'mock'`, `provider = 'mock'`; the output starts each paragraph with `[mock translation]` followed by deterministic Latin placeholder words of about the source length, so it differs from the input, passes the language, echo and ratio checks, and keeps the paragraph count. For the bundled sample articles a small fixture lexicon (same idea as the existing mock adapter, `src/lib/providers/mock.ts`) supplies readable English so graders can see the feature.
- UI: origin `mock` replaces the bar label with "Mock translation (no translation service configured)", and the "About this" panel says no external call was made. Search treats it like any translation, so it is searchable, but `matched_in` markers say "Matched in translation (mock)".
- Mock latency uses `MOCK_LATENCY_MS`; no budget is consumed (cost 0, `origin` mock), so grader runs never hit `deferred_budget`.

## 7. Deployment, upgrade, rollback and recovery
Upgrade from the current release (with data):
1. `git pull`, `docker compose build`.
2. `docker compose up -d`: `migrate` runs `0004`; `web` and `worker` restart on the new image. Ingestion through the web upload route pauses for the few seconds of the web restart; the upload endpoint is idempotent (devops 0002) and reconciliation shows no loss.
3. Existing foreign articles have no translation job. Backfill is optional and off by default (DBA 0003 section 10): a one-line SQL or a `--backfill-translations` option on the CLI queues jobs in batches of 1,000, paced by the budget. UNCONFIRMED whether the user wants it.
4. Verify: `/api/status` shows `translation` counts; open a foreign article; the dashboard row shows jobs moving.
Rollback:
- Fast stop without code change: `UPDATE system_flags SET value='false' WHERE key='translation_enabled'` (worker stops claiming; existing translations still display).
- Code rollback: redeploy the previous image. The old code ignores `translation` jobs, but the old worker's `claimJobs` filters by part, so they stay queued harmlessly; the new `ingest_new_version` signature breaks the old web image (it calls the old signature), so roll back web and worker together and run the DBA rollback script if the old signature must come back (DBA 0003 section 10).
- Data rollback: DBA rollback section; originals are untouched, so nothing is lost.
Backup/restore: `article_translations` is in the normal database backup; no extra step. Restore test checks translation counts and that the current-row unique index holds. Translations are re-creatable but cost money, so they are not excluded from backups.
Recovery after the provider is down: jobs go `failed_retryable` with backoff, the `openai-translate` breaker opens, jobs wait durably; on recovery the lane drains at `RPM_TRANSLATE` so catch-up cannot overwhelm the provider or the budget.

## 8. Host and platform settings
- Log rotation already set (`json-file`, 10 MB x 3). Translation adds few log lines (telemetry 0003 section 11); no change.
- Clock: translation lag SLO uses `ingested_at`, which is the database clock; no new dependency.
- Outbound network: the worker needs HTTPS to `api.openai.com` as today; if the host is offline, jobs stay queued, the breaker opens, and the mock mode (if selected) is the only offline option.
- DB pool: the worker's pool gets one more concurrent lane. After releasing the claim connection early (section 2) each lane holds a DB connection only for claim, save and cache writes. Set the worker pool max to at least `jev + openai + translate` concurrency plus 2; check the current value in `src/lib/db/pool.ts` before changing (UNCONFIRMED).

## 9. Deployment test plan
| Test | Proves | How | Pass |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| Clean bring-up | Zero-touch with migration `0004` | Fresh volumes, `docker compose up -d` with no `.env` | All healthy; `article_translations` exists; sample foreign articles get mock translations; `/api/status` shows `provider_mode=mock` |
| Real-key smoke | Real path | `.env` with a key and a small `BUDGET_TRANSLATE_DAILY`, upload `sample_articles.json` | Foreign articles translated (origin `provider`); spend recorded under `openai-translate`; page shows translation by default and the original on click |
| Idempotent restart | Re-run safe | `down` then `up`; `up` twice | Migration re-applies cleanly; no duplicate translations; jobs unchanged |
| Upgrade with data | `0004` on existing data | Start the previous release, load articles and results, upgrade | Existing articles, jobs, enrichments intact; new jobs for new foreign articles; search on originals unchanged |
| Constraint migration lock | FP-DB3 | Run `0004` against 1M `enrichment_jobs` rows while inserting | Insert stalls under 1 s |
| Kill switch | Operations | Set `translation_enabled=false`; upload foreign article | Job stays queued; page shows "Translation in progress"; flip back, it drains |
| Missing key, `auto` | ADR-0013 | No `OPENAI_API_KEY` | Mock lane, labelled everywhere; no outbound calls (check with egress block) |
| Missing key, `real` | Fast clear failure | `ENRICHMENT_MODE=real`, no key | Worker exits with a message naming `OPENAI_API_KEY` |
| Provider down | Resilience | Block egress to the provider for 10 min | Breaker `openai-translate` opens; sentiment and summaries unaffected; jobs resume after unblocking; alert T1 fires |
| Budget exhausted | ADR-0010 | `BUDGET_TRANSLATE_DAILY=0.01` | Jobs `deferred_budget`; summary lane unaffected; page shows the paused message |
| Worker crash mid-article | P2 | `docker kill` worker during a 15-chunk article | Claim expires, retry reuses cached chunks, exactly one current translation |
| Connection use | Section 2 finding | 2 long translations plus normal load; watch `pg_stat_activity` | Worker connections stay below pool max; none idle in transaction |
| Secret exposure | No leaks | `docker inspect`, `docker compose config`, log grep for the key and for sample article text | Key absent; no article text in logs |
| Alert and dashboard provisioning | Observability | `promtool check rules ops/alerts.yml`; open Grafana | Rules valid; row "Translation" present, no manual import |
| Capacity | Fit | PoC load with 30% foreign and the mock lane at 0 latency | Postgres CPU/IO within limits; translation lane keeps up |

## 10. Repository artefacts to create or change
- `db/migrations/0004_article_translations.sql` (DBA 0003).
- `src/lib/config.ts` and `.env.example` (section 6), `compose.yaml` (worker env lines), `compose.dev.yaml` if it duplicates worker env.
- `ops/alerts.yml` (T1 to T8), `ops/grafana/provisioning/dashboards/*.json` (translation row), `ops/prometheus.yml` only if a new job is needed (none).
- `src/worker/*` (translation lane, early release of the claim connection), `src/lib/providers/*` (translate adapter and mock), CLI option for backfill (optional).
- `README.md` / `docs/environment.md`: one paragraph on translation settings, mock mode, kill switch and rollback.
- CI: add `promtool check rules` and the clean-bring-up test to the existing pipeline if one exists (none found in the repository; UNCONFIRMED).

## 11. Risks and hot paths
| ID | Failure point | Effect | Principle | Detection |
| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
| FP-V1 | At the 800/s target, translating all foreign articles exceeds provider rate and budget | Permanent backlog, English search misses most foreign articles | P3 | Queue age, deferral counts (T1/T2); decision before scale-up |
| FP-V2 | Mock output mistaken for real translation | Readers trust placeholder text | P6, P7 | Origin `mock` label on page, `provider_mode` in status |
| FP-V3 | Worker holds a DB connection during long translations | Pool exhaustion, claims stall | P2 | Pool gauge, connection test |
| FP-V4 | Web and worker roll back separately across the `ingest_new_version` signature change | Upload route errors | P2 | Rollback instruction, smoke test after rollback |
| FP-V5 | Translation spend competes with summary spend | Core enrichment paused | P3 | Separate ledger key and cap |
| FP-V6 | `real` mode start with no key succeeds silently | No translation, no clue | P3 | Startup validation test |
| HP-V1 | Translation lane CPU for validators on long CJK text | Worker CPU | measure ms per 100 KB (HP-D1) |
| HP-V2 | Chunk cache writes | Small writes per chunk | measure with the crash test |

## 12. Handoff
- carma-backend-testing: reuse the Compose test environment; add the mock translator as the deterministic path and the failure-injection hooks (provider down, bad output) at the provider seam.
- carma-plan: order of work: migration and config first, worker connection fix, provider and mock, validators, then web.

## 13. Decisions needed and open questions
- Target hardware unknown. UNCONFIRMED.
- Whether to revisit ADR-0022 for any scale beyond the PoC (FP-V1): not needed now; flag for the user if the 800/s target becomes real.
- Translate-lane budget: default `3` (30% of the OpenAI cap) is a placeholder until prices are known.
- Backfill of existing foreign articles: default off.
- Worker pool max: check the current value.

Base directory for this skill: C:\Users\simon\AppData\Local\Claude-Data\claude_pzs8sxrjxfjjc\local-agent-mode-sessions\skills-plugin\1cec5490-7429-4b0e-9f4f-735b92a256c6\9696b3ec-826e-4b0c-b0c0-25f9eaf3187d\skills\carma-backend-testing

# carma-backend-testing

In this pipeline the most dangerous bug is the silent one: an article that goes in and never comes out, comes out altered, or arrives after the window. Ordinary functional tests rarely catch it. This skill plans tests that prove **no data is lost or corrupted between stages**, and that the **soft requirements** (time taken, load handled) are met with evidence rather than assertion.

The output is a plan, not test code. Only write tests if the user asks for them as a follow-up.

Read `references/carma-context.md` first for the principles, constraints and spec conventions.

## Inputs

Read the latest non-superseded specs for the same feature: `.specs/architect/` (data flow, states, FP and HP registers), `.specs/data/dba/` (schema, write path, verification plan), and, if present, `.specs/search/` (recall evaluation plan), `.specs/data/sanitization/` (security test inputs), `.specs/telemetry/` (signals tests can assert on) and `.specs/devops/` (the Compose stack the tests run against, and the deployment tests that carma-devops already covers: clean bring-up, upgrade, backup and restore, secrets). Do not duplicate those; use the same disposable Compose environment for integration, load and fault tests. The FP registers across those specs are the backbone of this plan: each failure point must map to at least one test. Each HP entry must map to a measurement. If the architect or DBA spec is missing, say so and ask.

Inspect the codebase for how tests are done today: language, framework, runner, fixtures, whether integration tests use a real database, existing load tooling and CI configuration. Match what is there; recommend new tooling only where a real gap exists. Record paths. Check `.benchmarks/` too: quick Node.js benchmarks written by carma-benchmark cover single changes; this plan covers the full suite, soak and fault tests. Reuse their generator and thresholds where they exist so the numbers agree, and do not duplicate them.

## Workflow

### 1. Data integrity and completeness across stages

Define the invariants first, then the tests that attack them.

- **Conservation.** For a controlled input set, every article is accounted for at every stage boundary: `received = indexed + rejected + quarantined + dead-lettered + duplicate`, each with a reason. No stage may change the total silently. Specify the reconciliation query or check at each boundary and run it after every scenario.
- **Fidelity.** An article's text content is stored faithfully (compare hashes of the extracted text end to end), the reduction of any markup to text is recorded as a transformation, and derived fields reference their source. Include a round trip through storage and search for English, Arabic and Chinese, with right-to-left text, mixed scripts, emoji, combining characters, very long bodies, and characters that tend to break things (NUL, zero-width, bidirectional controls). Add markup-to-text cases: nested tags, scripts and styles, HTML entities, hidden elements, and Arabic and Chinese text inside markup.
- **Idempotency.** Delivering the same article twice, or reprocessing a batch, produces the same state and no duplicates. Reordering and late arrival do not corrupt state.
- **Ledger correctness.** Processing-state records match reality: nothing stuck "in progress" after a worker dies, nothing marked done that is not.
- **Confidence and lineage (P6, P7, P8).** Every derived value has a normalised confidence in 0 to 100, with raw value, range, origin and method recorded; normalisation is correct at the boundaries of each scorer's min and max; values that cannot be scored show "no confidence available" rather than a number.
- **Search completeness (P3).** Planted mentions in each language are found (from the searchability evaluation plan), and an article that is stored is searchable once its state says so.

### 2. Failure-point coverage

Build a table that traces every FP entry (from the architect, searchability, DBA and data-sanity specs) to the tests that exercise it. For each, choose the technique that fits:

- Fault injection: kill a worker mid-batch, drop the database connection, fail over the database, exhaust the connection pool, stall a dependency, return garbage from the scorer, fill the disk, skew the clock.
- Poison and malformed input: invalid or oversized fields, missing or future `published_at`, duplicate ids, unsupported language, hostile content from the data-sanity spec.
- Backpressure and recovery: a backlog builds, then clears; catch-up must exceed the arrival rate.
- Expected outcome for each: the recorded reason, the metric or log that appears, and the state the system returns to.

An FP with no test is a gap; list it and say why or what is needed.

### 3. Soft requirements: profile and prove

State each as a measurable claim with a threshold, a method and the evidence kept.

- **Freshness.** From `published_at` to searchable and to delivered for a mention: the share within 15 minutes and the p50, p95, p99 and maximum, under sustained load. The only agreed target is 15 minutes; any other threshold is proposed and labelled so.
- **Throughput.** 800 articles a second sustained for a long enough soak to expose leaks, bloat and checkpoint effects (duration chosen to span several autovacuum and checkpoint cycles), plus peak and burst profiles above the base rate.
- **Load shapes.** Steady, ramp, burst, backlog-then-recover, and mixed search plus ingestion (reads must not starve writes, and the reverse).
- **Resource behaviour.** CPU, memory, connections, WAL rate, replication lag and index size under load, so capacity headroom is known.
- **Latency of interfaces.** Request and response times per endpoint and per key query, with percentiles rather than averages.
- **Hot paths.** For each HP entry, a measurement (profile, query plan, microbenchmark, or load test slice) and what result would trigger the human inspection the architect asked for. This is the interim performance coverage until a dedicated performance skill exists.
- **Language mix.** Load tests use realistic proportions of English, Arabic and Chinese, since analysis cost differs by language.

Specify the load generator: it produces articles in the agreed schema with seeded randomness (reproducible), realistic size distribution, planted mentions at a known rate, duplicates and late arrivals at a known rate, and a controllable language mix. Results are recorded with environment details (hardware, database settings, version, data volume), because a performance number without its environment cannot be compared or trusted.

### 4. Resilience and negative testing

The architect's resilience design (retry policies, circuit breakers, bulkheads, dead-letter handling, degraded modes) is a set of promises. This step plans tests that try to break each one. Start from the per-dependency table in that spec; if it is missing, say so and derive the dependencies from the FP register.

**Negative testing principles.** Test what must not happen as deliberately as what must. For every function and boundary: invalid, missing, null, oversized, malformed, wrongly typed, out-of-range and out-of-order input; duplicates; unexpected state (acting on an item that is already done, locked or gone); unauthorised or expired credentials; and boundary values on both sides of every limit. Each negative test states the expected safe outcome: rejected or quarantined with a recorded reason, a clear error, no partial writes, no data loss, no crash, and no secret or stack trace leaked. Cover every row of the null matrix from the data-sanity spec when it exists.

**Dependency failure modes.** For each dependency, inject each of: connection refused, timeout (slow but not dead), slow responses that push latency past the threshold, intermittent errors at a controlled rate, hard 4xx and 5xx responses, rate limiting with `Retry-After`, malformed or truncated responses, valid-looking but wrong responses (a score outside its range, an unsupported language), partial success in a batch, and an outage that lasts longer than the retry window. Use a controllable fake or fault-injection proxy so failures are reproducible, and keep the real dependency out of the loop.

**Retry behaviour.** Verify: transient failures retry and eventually succeed; permanent failures do not retry past the first classification; the attempt count, backoff growth and jitter match the policy (assert on timing distribution, not exact values); the per-attempt timeout and overall deadline are honoured; the retry budget caps amplification (a downstream outage must not multiply load); retried operations are idempotent (no duplicates, no double counting, no double spend on a paid API); retries survive a worker crash because their state is in the database; and an item that exceeds its attempts reaches the dead-letter state with the reason recorded.

**Circuit breaker behaviour.** Verify: the breaker opens at the configured threshold and not before; while open, calls fail fast without hitting the dependency; the declared degraded mode runs (work queued durably, or enrichment skipped and marked) and no item is dropped or shown with a default as if it were a result; it half-opens after the cool-down with limited probes; it closes only after success and reopens on failure (no flapping); one dependency's breaker does not affect another; the breaker state is visible in telemetry and alerts fire; and the backlog built during the outage drains after recovery faster than new arrivals without causing a second failure.

**Permanent failure handling.** Verify dead-letter and quarantine entries carry reason, attempts, last error and timestamps; replay after a fix works, is rate-limited and idempotent; reconciliation totals still balance with dead-lettered items counted; a source that stays unreachable produces a visible coverage gap rather than silence; and operators can see and act on the situation from telemetry alone.

**Resilience under load and combination.** Repeat the key scenarios at 800 articles a second, since behaviour at idle proves little (retry storms, pool exhaustion and queue growth only appear under load), and in combination (a scorer outage during a database failover, a backlog during a source burst). Include a recovery test that confirms the system returns to its normal steady state without manual intervention. Run the experiments as scheduled game days with a defined blast radius, a steady-state hypothesis stated first and abort conditions.

Where behaviour depends on a threshold (breaker trip rate, attempts, backoff cap), test the configured values and also check that changing them in configuration actually changes the behaviour.

### 5. Test levels and placement

Assign each test to a level so the fast suite stays fast:

- Unit tests for pure logic (normalisation, validation, score scaling).
- Integration tests against a real PostgreSQL (not a mock; partitioning, locking and index behaviour only show up on the real thing), using disposable instances.
- Contract tests for the article schema and for any external scorer or model interface.
- End-to-end pipeline tests for conservation and fidelity on small sets.

# carma-plan

The other skills each look at one concern. This one looks across them. Its value is in what no single spec can see: where two specs disagree, where one assumes something another never provides, and what order the work has to happen in so each step can be verified. A plan that merely concatenates the specs hides those problems until execution, when they cost the most.

The plan must be usable by someone who has not read the specs: each task says what to do, where, with what inputs, and how to know it is done.

Read `references/carma-context.md` first for the principles, constraints and spec conventions.

## Inputs

Inventory what exists for the feature by listing, and reading the latest non-superseded spec in, each of:

- `.specs/architect/` and `.specs/architect/adrs/` (design, decisions, FP and HP registers)
- `.specs/search/`
- `.specs/telemetry/`
- `.specs/data/sanitization/`
- `.specs/data/dba/`
- `.specs/testing/backend/`
- `.specs/ux/`
- `.specs/devops/` (Compose topology, secrets, bring-up, deployment tests)
- earlier plans in `.specs/plan/` for the same feature

Report which are present and which are missing, and for each missing one say whether the feature needs it (the architect spec's downstream handoff says which skills apply). A missing spec that the feature needs is an open question, not something to fill with guesses. If nothing exists at all, say so and recommend starting with carma-architect.

Approved ADRs are decisions. Specs marked `UNCONFIRMED` or listing open decisions are not. Plan around the decided ones and surface the rest.

## Workflow

### 1. Consistency review

Before writing tasks, read the specs against each other and the context file. Look for:

- **Contradictions.** For example, the DBA plan relaxes durability while the architect spec requires no loss; the search design needs an extension the environment may not allow; the UX needs a field no spec produces; telemetry labels with high cardinality; a testing threshold that differs from the architect's.
- **Gaps.** A failure point (FP-n) with no test, a hot path (HP-n) with no measurement, a signal with no emitter, a table with no migration, a screen with no data source.
- **Unvalidated assumptions** from the context file's known unknowns (`published_at` accuracy, id uniqueness, Postgres version and extensions, size and mix of articles) that a design silently depends on.
- **Principle conflicts.** Where a choice trades P3 completeness, P2 reliability or P6 to P8 transparency for speed, and no decision records it.
- **Unmade decisions.** Open questions in any spec.

Classify each finding as a **blocker** (must be resolved before the affected work starts), a **risk** (proceed but track) or a **note**. For each blocker name who can resolve it and what the options are. If blockers need the user, ask now using the protocol in the context file; otherwise record them at the top of the plan.

### 2. Break the work into tasks

Create tasks that a human or agent can pick up and complete without further interpretation. Each task has:

- **ID and title** (verb first)
- **Why**: the requirement, decision (ADR number) or failure point it serves, and principles
- **Steps**: ordered, concrete actions
- **Where**: files, modules, tables or systems touched, with paths from the codebase analysis
- **Inputs and outputs**: what must exist before, what exists after
- **Acceptance criteria**: observable checks, including the test or measurement from the testing spec that proves it
- **Estimate**: hours as a range
- **Depends on**: task IDs
- **Owner type**: `agent`, `human`, or `either`, with the reason when `human` (a decision, a hot-path inspection the architect flagged, an approval, access to an environment)
- **Spec references**: the sections it implements

Include the tasks people forget: environments and test data, migrations and their rollbacks, the load generator and harness, telemetry emission, dashboards and alerts, security hardening, documentation of decisions. Human gates from the architect's hot path register become explicit tasks, not footnotes.

### 3. Order by dependency

Build the dependency graph and check it has no cycles. Derive the order from the graph, not from the order the specs were written. Identify the critical path and the work that can run in parallel, and say which parallel work needs different people or agents.

Prefer a **walking skeleton** early, starting from a single `docker compose up` that brings up the empty stack healthy (database, migrations, one worker, observability), then the thinnest end-to-end path (one article from ingestion through storage, search and telemetry) before widening any stage. It proves the pieces fit while changes are still cheap, and it gives the testing and telemetry work something real to measure. After each phase that changes a hot path, schedule a quick benchmark task (carma-benchmark) and a review task (carma-review) as a gate before the next phase, and say who runs them. Put risky unknowns (extension availability, write throughput, language analysis) early so they fail cheaply.

### 4. Group into phases

Decide how many phases the project needs. A phase should take roughly 8 to 16 hours of focused work (one to two days) executed end to end, and should end in something verifiable. Size by summing task estimates; split a phase that runs past 16 hours and merge ones under about 8 unless a dependency boundary forces them apart. Say if the estimates carry large uncertainty.

Each phase has:

- **Goal** in one sentence
- **Entry criteria** (what must be true to start, including resolved blockers)
- **Tasks** in execution order, with owner types
- **Exit criteria** (what is verified, by which test or measurement)
- **Total estimate** and the largest uncertainty in it
- **Rollback or safe-stop**: what state the system is in if work stops here
- **Human checkpoints**: decisions or inspections needed within the phase

A phase boundary should be a place where it is safe to pause and review.

### 5. Execution notes

Add what a person or agent running the plan needs: how to work through tasks and report status, what to do when a task's assumption turns out false (stop and raise it, do not improvise a design change), and when to return to a design skill (for example if measurements break a throughput assumption, rerun carma-architect or carma-dba with the new evidence).

## Output

Write the plan with these sections, in this order. Put the consistency findings first so nobody starts work on top of an unresolved blocker:

1. **Summary** (what is being built, number of phases, total estimate, critical path in one line)
2. **Inputs** (specs and ADRs used, with paths; missing specs and whether needed)
3. **Blockers and open questions** (must be actioned before execution; each with owner and options)
4. **Consistency report** (contradictions, gaps, unvalidated assumptions, principle conflicts; classified as blocker, risk or note)
5. **Dependency graph** (table of task dependencies plus a Mermaid or text diagram; critical path and parallel tracks marked)
6. **Phases** (each as described in step 4, with its tasks written out in full as in step 2)
7. **Traceability matrix** (requirement or FP/HP to task to test or measurement; any row with an empty cell is a gap)
8. **Risks and assumptions** (including the estimate uncertainty)
9. **Execution notes**

For a large plan, keep the overview in the main file and put each phase's full task detail in a section that is easy to link to, rather than splitting the plan across files that can drift apart.

## Persisting the work (when run inside a codebase)

If executed in a codebase, the output of this skill is numbered as a sequence in `.specs/plan`. Follow "Spec conventions" in the context file: number with `python scripts/next_spec_number.py .specs/plan`, write `.specs/plan/NNNN-<feature-slug>.md` with `spec: carma-plan` front matter and list every spec and ADR you used under `inputs`. Edit in place while `draft`. Once a plan is `approved`, a revised plan is a new numbered file with `supersedes` set, so the history of what was agreed stays intact. When a blocker is resolved by a human decision that should be binding, suggest recording it as an ADR through carma-architect and reference its number in the plan.

If you are not in a codebase, deliver the output in the conversation and offer to save it.

groups:
  - name: media-signal
    rules:
      - alert: WorkerHeartbeatStale
        expr: time() - mss_worker_heartbeat_unixtime > 120
        for: 2m
        labels:
          severity: warning
        annotations:
          summary: Worker heartbeat is stale
      - alert: EnrichmentBacklogHigh
        expr: mss_jobs_queued > 100
        for: 10m
        labels:
          severity: warning
        annotations:
          summary: Enrichment job backlog is high

  - name: media-signal-uploads
    rules:
      - alert: UploadReconcileMismatch
        expr: increase(mss_upload_reconcile_mismatch_total[1h]) > 0
        for: 0m
        labels:
          severity: page
        annotations:
          summary: Upload reconcile mismatch detected (U1)
      - alert: UploadErrorRateHigh
        expr: |
          (
            sum(rate(mss_upload_requests_total{outcome="error"}[30m]))
            /
            clamp_min(sum(rate(mss_upload_requests_total[30m])), 1e-9)
          ) > 0.05
        for: 30m
        labels:
          severity: ticket
        annotations:
          summary: Upload 5xx ratio above 5% (U2)

---
spec: carma-plan
number: 0003
title: Execution plan for article translation
status: draft
date: 2026-10-24
feature: article-translation
inputs: [.specs/architect/0003-article-translation.md, .specs/architect/adrs/0022-translate-at-ingest-as-enrichment-part.md, .specs/architect/adrs/0023-openai-small-model-chunked-translation.md, .specs/architect/adrs/0024-translation-no-confidence-article-page-only.md, .specs/architect/adrs/0025-search-covers-original-and-translated-text.md, .specs/architect/adrs/0026-english-headline-on-all-foreign-cards.md, .specs/architect/adrs/0027-search-not-original-only-and-trigram-on-translations.md, .specs/architect/adrs/0028-no-backfill-of-existing-foreign-articles.md, .specs/search/0002-article-translation.md, .specs/data/sanitization/0003-article-translation.md, .specs/data/dba/0003-article-translation.md, .specs/telemetry/0003-article-translation.md, .specs/ux/0003-article-translation.md, .specs/devops/0003-article-translation.md, .specs/testing/backend/0003-article-translation.md]
principles: [P1, P2, P3, P5, P6, P7, P8]
supersedes: null
---

# 0003 Execution plan for article translation

## 1. Summary
Build: for non-English articles, translate headline and body to English at ingest through a third enrichment part, show the translation by default with a "Show original" toggle, and make search match both texts. Eight phases, about 90 to 120 hours in total (large uncertainty in the worker and UI phases, section 8). Critical path: schema (P1) → enqueue (P2) → worker lane core (P3) → save, cache and budget (P4) → UI (P6) → hardening (P8). Search (P5) and telemetry (P7) can run in parallel after P4's save path exists.

## 2. Inputs
All eight article-translation specs and ADR-0022 to ADR-0028 listed in the front matter are present and read; earlier plans 0001 and 0002 were used only for conventions. No spec is missing: searchability, data-sanity, DBA, telemetry, UX, devops and testing all ran. Nothing was skipped by choice. `AGENTS.md` applies to every task that touches Next.js code: read the relevant guide in `node_modules/next/dist/docs/` first (route handlers, client components, server components), because this Next version differs from common knowledge.

## 3. Blockers and open questions
| ID | Item | Blocks | Owner | Options |
| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
| B1 | OpenAI model id and prices are still unset (ADR-0003). Real-mode cost cap, the real-model sample (testing 0003 FP-D2/D3 calibration) and the budget cap cannot be finalised | T8.3, T8.4; not P1 to P7 (the mock path works) | User | Supply `OPENAI_MODEL` and prices; or accept mock-only verification and finish T8.3 later |
| B2 | Translate budget: devops 0003 adds a separate ledger key `openai-translate` with its own cap (default 3), sanitization 0003 and ADR-0023 call it "a share of the OpenAI budget". Separate keys make total OpenAI spend = 10 + 3 unless the existing cap is lowered | T1.3 (defaults), T4.3 | User | (a) additive: total ceiling 13 per day; (b) carve-out: `BUDGET_OPENAI_DAILY` 7 + translate 3 = 10; (c) one shared key (translation can starve summaries; rejected by FP-8) |
| B3 | The telemetry specs treat many series as "existing" that the code does not emit (section 4, C2). Scope of P7 depends on this | T7.1 | User or lead | (a) implement the baseline set needed by the translation alerts only (planned); (b) implement all of telemetry 0001 first (separate feature) |
| B4 | Target hardware unknown (carried over from devops 0001/0002) | T8.5 capacity runs only | User | Provide specs; or run on a dev machine and label results |
Open but not blocking (defaults taken, listed as risks): reveal-beacon build-or-skip (default build, T6.7 is last and can be dropped), sticky toggle (default no), superseded-translation retention 30 days, log sampling of `translation.accepted`, SLO numbers, chunk size, max chunks and ratio bounds, whether `trgm_index` is on in the target database.
FP-V1 (translating every foreign article is infeasible at the 800/s target) is a recorded risk, not a blocker; ADR-0022 should be revisited as hybrid before any scale-up.

## 4. Consistency report
Cross-checked against the spec text and the code.
| ID | Finding | Class | Resolution |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| C1 | Devops 0003 says web readiness checks `/api/health`; the code has `/api/healthz` and `/api/readyz` (`src/app/api/readyz/route.ts`, which checks `schema_migrations`) | Note | Extend `readyz` to check `to_regclass('article_translations')`; use the real route names in docs (T6.8) |
| C2 | Telemetry 0003 reuses "existing" series (`mss_jobs`, `mss_job_outcomes_total`, `mss_job_oldest_age_seconds`, `mss_time_to_enriched_seconds`, `mss_budget_deferred_total`, `mss_prompt_injection_suspected_total`, `mss_db_query_duration_seconds`, `mss_http_request_duration_seconds`, `mss_search_duration_seconds`, `mss_breaker_state`, `mss_llm_cost_micro_total`, `mss_provider_duration_seconds`, `mss_ingest_duration_seconds`). The code emits only upload series, `mss_event_loop_lag_seconds`, `mss_worker_heartbeat_unixtime` and build info; `ops/alerts.yml` already references `mss_jobs_queued` and `mss_job_oldest_age_seconds`, which nothing emits | Blocker for P7 scope (B3) | T7.1 implements the minimal baseline (job gauges per `part`/`state`, outcome counter, provider duration, budget deferrals, breaker state) the translation alerts rely on |
| C3 | Telemetry T-SLI-1 uses `translation job succeeded_at`; `enrichment_jobs` has no such column, and `articles.ingested_at` stays the first arrival for later versions (DBA 0002) | Risk | Define lag as `article_translations.created_at − (CASE WHEN version = 1 THEN ingested_at ELSE updated_at END)`; no schema change (T7.2) |
| C4 | Untranslated count: telemetry `mss_search_foreign_untranslated` is global and refreshed every 60 s; the UX note and search spec need the count for the current selection | Note | Two different things. Keep the gauge; compute the per-request count in the search query (T5.4) |
| C5 | Reason codes differ by spec: sanitization `out_echo`, `out_wrong_lang`…; telemetry labels `echo`, `wrong_lang`…; UX copy covers three failure messages while telemetry lists `attempts` and `budget_never` as dead reasons with no copy | Risk | One enum in code (`src/lib/translate/reasons.ts`, T1.2) mapping job reason, metric label and UI copy key; add copy for `attempts` ("Translation unavailable: the service kept failing") and `budget_never` |
| C6 | Sanitization 0003 section 9 says validated chunks are cached in the job's raw output / `origin=cache`; DBA 0003 creates `translation_chunk_cache` | Note | DBA table governs; `origin='cache'` only labels metrics/rows produced from cache hits (T4.2) |
| C7 | `enrichments.raw_output jsonb` would store the full model response for translation, duplicating the entire translated text and putting article text in a second place | Risk | For `translation`, store only `{usage, model_reported, chunk_count}` in `raw_output` (T4.1); sanitization says logs never hold text, this extends it to the DB |
| C8 | Worker pool max is 6 (`src/lib/db/pool.ts:16`); the claim loop holds one pooled client across provider calls (`src/worker/loop.ts`) | Risk | Release the claim client right after COMMIT (T3.1), then set pool max to lanes + 2 (T3.1) |
| C9 | NOT semantics: ADR-0027 (original side only) replaced the default in search 0002, DBA 0003 and UX 0003; testing 0003 updated; no remaining text checked contradicts it | Note | Verified after the patch; test row in testing 0003 section 8.3 |
| C10 | ADR-0027 builds a trigram index on translations, but `articles_trgm_idx` creation is guarded by a `trgm_index` flag (can be `off`) (`0001_init.sql:179-188`) | Risk | Migration guards the same way; compiler reads the flag and still works (sequential ILIKE) when off (T1.4, T5.1) |
| C11 | ADR-0028 (no backfill) means after release every older foreign article counts as "not translated"; the UX note turns warn-style above 5% and would be permanently alarming | Risk | Count and label "older articles, not scheduled" as a separate reason that does not trigger the warn style (T5.4, T6.5) |
| C12 | Mock translation must pass the output validators (language check for Latin-script sources uses an English stop-word ratio; ratio bounds; paragraph count) | Risk | Mock builds output from common English words in the right paragraph structure with `[mock translation]` prefix, verified by running the validators in a unit test (T3.4) |
| C13 | `isEnglish` rule: spec says `en`/`en-*`; real data may carry `EN`, `en_US`, `eng` | Note | Normalise case, split on `-`/`_`, accept primary tag `en` or `eng`; unknown/empty stays "needs translation" (T1.2). The decision is passed from TypeScript to SQL as a boolean so the rule exists once |
| C14 | Migration numbering `0004`, enqueue statement count (three jobs in one multi-row INSERT), route name `/api/telemetry/translation-view` and label keys `script`, `view` (must be added to `ALLOWED_LABEL_KEYS` and `tests/unit/metrics-labels.test.ts`) agree across DBA, devops, telemetry, testing | Note | Verified; T1.3/T7.3 carry the label allow-list change |
| C15 | `ingest_new_version` signature change breaks an old web image that still calls the old signature; web and worker must deploy together | Risk | Drop the old overload; deploy both images in one `docker compose up -d`; rollback instructions in devops 0003 section 7 (T2.1, T8.6) |
| C16 | UX says both texts are in the HTML and JS-disabled fallback is undecided (testing 0003 lists it as a gap) | Note | Default: server HTML shows the translation and puts the original in a collapsed `<details>`; the client component takes over after hydration (T6.2) |
| C17 | No CI exists, so the MUST tier (testing 0003 section 10) has no runner | Risk | Optional task T8.7 adds a minimal workflow; a human decides |
| C18 | FP coverage gaps: FP-9 (language mislabel) and FP-V1 (scale) have no automated test | Note | Accepted (testing 0003 section 12); manual sample in T8.4 |
| C19 | Principle check: nothing here trades P3, P2 or P6 to P8 for speed. The one P3 cost is that English search misses foreign articles until translated, which the UI states (UX section 6) | Note | Recorded; no extra decision needed |

## 5. Dependency graph
```mermaid
flowchart LR
  T1.1 --> T1.2 --> T1.3 --> T1.4 --> T1.5
  T1.5 --> T2.1 --> T2.3 --> T2.4
  T1.2 --> T2.2 --> T2.3
  T2.1 --> T3.1 --> T3.2 --> T3.3 --> T3.4
  T3.4 --> T4.1 --> T4.2 --> T4.3 --> T4.5
  T4.1 --> T4.4 --> T4.5
  T4.1 --> T5.1 --> T5.2 --> T5.3 --> T5.4
  T4.1 --> T6.1 --> T6.2 --> T6.3
  T5.2 --> T6.4
  T5.4 --> T6.5
  T6.3 --> T6.6 --> T6.7
  T4.5 --> T7.1 --> T7.2 --> T7.3 --> T7.4
  T6.7 --> T8.1
  T7.4 --> T8.1
  T5.4 --> T8.1
  T8.1 --> T8.2 --> T8.3 --> T8.4
  T8.2 --> T8.5 --> T8.6
```
Critical path: T1.1 → T1.4 → T2.1 → T3.1 to T3.4 → T4.1 → T6.1 → T6.3 → T6.7 → T8.1 to T8.6. Parallel tracks after T4.1: search (P5, needs compiler knowledge), UI (P6, needs a data shape), telemetry (P7). P5 and P6 touch different files except `ArticleCard.tsx` and the search route (T5.2 before T6.4).
Gates: after P2, P4 and P5 run carma-benchmark (HP-1, HP-S1) and carma-review before the next phase starts (agent runs benchmark; a human reads the plan comparison in T5.3).

## 6. Phases

### Phase 1: Decisions, helpers, configuration and schema (≈10 to 14 h)
Goal: the database has the translation schema and the code has configuration and shared helpers, with nothing yet enqueued.
Entry: B2 answered (T1.1). 
Exit: `0004` applies cleanly on an empty database and on a populated one, re-applies safely, rollback dry-run works; config validates; unit tests for helpers pass.
Rollback/safe-stop: nothing behaves differently until P2; dropping the new tables restores the old state.
Human checkpoints: T1.1 (decision), review of the migration (T1.4).

**T1.1 Resolve B2 and record it.** Why: ADR-0010, spend control (P2). Steps: ask the user B2; if a decision is made, record an ADR via carma-architect; set the defaults in T1.3 accordingly. Where: `.specs/architect/adrs/`. Accept: ADR number noted in the plan. Estimate: 0.5 to 1 h. Depends: none. Owner: human (decision). Specs: devops 0003 s6, sanitization 0003 s9.

**T1.2 Add shared translation helpers.** Why: single source of truth for the language rule and reason codes (C5, C13). Steps: create `src/lib/translate/language.ts` (`isEnglish`, `needsTranslation`), `src/lib/translate/reasons.ts` (enum with job reason, metric label, UI copy key), types for the translation part; extend `src/lib/reasons.ts` if it already holds reason codes (read it first). Where: `src/lib/translate/*`, `tests/unit/translate-language.test.ts`. Accept: table tests for `en`, `EN`, `en-GB`, `en_US`, `eng`, `ar`, `zh-Hans`, empty, null, `"N/A"`; reasons enum covers all sanitization and telemetry codes. Estimate: 1.5 to 2.5 h. Depends: T1.1. Owner: agent. Specs: search/sanitization 0003 s3, UX s5.

**T1.3 Add configuration.** Why: devops 0003 s6. Steps: add the variables to the zod schema in `src/lib/config.ts` with ranges (`TRANSLATE_RATIO_*` parsed from "min,max", min < max), add to the typed config object, `.env.example`, `compose.yaml` worker env (and `compose.dev.yaml` if it duplicates env), `docs/environment.md`; add `script` and `view` to `ALLOWED_LABEL_KEYS` and update `tests/unit/metrics-labels.test.ts` and `tests/unit/config.test.ts`. Where: `src/lib/config.ts`, `src/lib/metrics.ts`, `.env.example`, `compose*.yaml`, `docs/environment.md`. Accept: bad values fail with the variable name; defaults match devops 0003 s6; `ENRICHMENT_MODE=real` without a key still fails fast. Estimate: 1.5 to 2.5 h. Depends: T1.2. Owner: agent.

**T1.4 Write migration `0004_article_translations.sql`.** Why: DBA 0003 s4, s7, s10. Steps: (1) drop and re-add the two `part` CHECKs, looking constraint names up in `pg_constraint`, using `NOT VALID` then `VALIDATE`; (2) create `article_translations` with the columns in DBA 0003 s4 (no confidence columns), the CHECK `at_has_text`, `fillfactor 90`, autovacuum settings; (3) partial unique index `article_translations_current_uq`, partial GIN on `search_vector`, partial trigram GIN guarded by the `trgm_index` flag (same pattern as `0001_init.sql:179-188`), built `CONCURRENTLY` is not possible inside the migration transaction, so create it with the table (empty); (4) `translation_chunk_cache`; (5) grants from DBA 0003 s10 (app_read SELECT on `article_translations`, app_worker SELECT/INSERT plus `UPDATE (superseded_at)`, cache table to app_worker only); (6) seed `system_flags` `translation_enabled` from the setting in `src/cli/migrate.ts` next to `enrichment_enabled`; (7) write the manual rollback as a comment block at the top like `0003`. Where: `db/migrations/0004_article_translations.sql`, `src/cli/migrate.ts`. Accept: applies on an empty database and on a database at `0003` with data; second run is a no-op; `\d` shows the indexes; grants verified by attempting forbidden writes as each role. Estimate: 3 to 4 h. Depends: T1.3. Owner: agent, human review (migration review). Specs: DBA 0003 s4, s7, s10; devops s5.

**T1.5 Test the migration.** Why: FP-DB3, FP-DB6. Steps: integration test applying `0003` then `0004` on a seeded database; check constraints, indexes, grants per role, idempotent re-run; a test that the migration file contains no non-concurrent index creation on existing populated tables (static grep); measure the constraint swap with 1M job rows (run once, record the lock time, `tests/integration/migration-0004.test.ts`). Accept: lock time under 1 s at 1M rows. Estimate: 2.5 to 3.5 h. Depends: T1.4. Owner: agent. Specs: testing 0003 FP-DB3, devops s9.

### Phase 2: Enqueue on ingest and test fixtures (≈10 to 14 h)
Goal: every non-English article (new or re-versioned) gets exactly one translation job; ingest throughput is unchanged.
Entry: P1 exit.
Exit: I1 (enqueue half), I4, FP-1 and FP-DB1 tests pass; HP-1 benchmark within 5%; carma-review done.
Rollback/safe-stop: jobs just sit queued with no worker lane; turn off by not deploying P3 or by `translation_enabled=false`.
Human checkpoint: review of the changed hot path (architect HP-1).

**T2.1 Change the enqueue in `ingestOne` and `ingest_new_version`.** Why: ADR-0022, DBA 0003 s4. Steps: in `src/lib/ingest/ingest.ts` (around line 525) replace the per-part loop with one multi-row INSERT building the rows `sentiment`, `summary_topics` and, when `needsTranslation(language)` and there is text, `translation` (`skipped_no_content` state when no text, same rule as today); in a new migration step inside `0004` (or a function-replace block at its end) `CREATE OR REPLACE` `ingest_new_version` with the new parameter `p_needs_translation boolean`, which supersedes the current translation row and inserts the new job; drop the old overload and re-grant EXECUTE with the full argument list; update the TypeScript caller. Where: `src/lib/ingest/ingest.ts`, `db/migrations/0004_*.sql`. Accept: statements per admitted article do not increase; both paths covered by tests; `\df` shows one overload. Estimate: 3 to 4 h. Depends: T1.5, T1.2. Owner: agent, human review. Specs: DBA 0003 s4, FP-1, FP-DB1, HP-1.

**T2.2 Build fakes and fixtures.** Why: testing 0003 s2, s7. Steps: `tests/fakes/translator.ts` (modes listed in testing 0003 s2, records calls per chunk), `tests/fixtures/translation.ts` (ar, zh, fr, en, unknown, mixed, long 1/20/21 chunks, injection, no headline, no body), extend `tests/fixtures/articles.ts` only if needed. Accept: fixtures load through `loadArticles`; the fake's modes are unit-tested. Estimate: 2 to 3 h. Depends: T1.2. Owner: agent.

**T2.3 Write enqueue integration tests.** Why: I1 (enqueue part), I2, I4, I11, FP-1, FP-DB1. Steps: tests for each language row, new version path with and without the flag, duplicate ingest, old overload absent, `skipped_no_content`, reconciliation query (the telemetry T4 query as a SQL helper `tests/harness/translation-ledger.ts`). Where: `tests/integration/translation-enqueue.test.ts`. Accept: all green against a real Postgres. Estimate: 3 to 4 h. Depends: T2.1, T2.2. Owner: agent.

**T2.4 Benchmark and review gate.** Why: HP-1/HP-DB1, ADR-0022 cost. Steps: add `--foreign-share` to `.benchmarks/article-ingest/bench.mjs`; run 100,000 articles at 0% and 30% foreign (carma-benchmark); run carma-review on the diff; record results under `reports/`. Accept: rows/s with 30% foreign within 5% of 0%; review has no blocker. Estimate: 2 to 3 h. Depends: T2.3. Owner: agent runs, human reads. 

### Phase 3: Worker lane core (≈13 to 16 h)
Goal: the worker can translate one article correctly (chunk, call provider or mock, validate), without yet saving.
Entry: P2 exit. Read `src/worker/*` fully first.
Exit: unit tests for chunker, validators, mock and provider adapter pass; claim connection fix in place.
Rollback/safe-stop: lane disabled by default flag until P4.
Human checkpoint: T3.3 regex review (HP-D1).

**T3.1 Unify the part type, free the claim connection, size the pool.** Why: C8, FP-V3. Steps: introduce `type EnrichmentPart = "sentiment" | "summary_topics" | "translation"` and use it in `claim.ts`, `finish.ts`, `loop.ts`; in `loop.ts` release the claim `client` immediately after `COMMIT` and before processing jobs; extend the part loop with a `translation` lane with its own breaker (`openai-translate`), concurrency, RPM and the `translation_enabled` flag check; set worker pool max to `jev + openai + translate concurrency + 2` (`src/lib/db/pool.ts`). Where: `src/worker/*.ts`, `src/lib/db/pool.ts`. Accept: existing worker tests still pass; new test shows no connection held during a 5 s fake call. Estimate: 3 to 4 h. Depends: T2.1. Owner: agent, human review.

**T3.2 Write the chunker and the translation prompt.** Why: ADR-0023, sanitization s5, s8. Steps: `src/lib/translate/chunk.ts` (paragraph split, sentence split for long paragraphs, grapheme-safe last resort, chunk size from config, count cap → `too_long`); `src/lib/translate/prompt.ts` (nonce fence reused from `src/lib/enrich/prompt.ts`, system prompt: translate only, leave names and numbers, plain text, JSON `{translation, detected_language}`, one output paragraph per input paragraph); strip bidi override and zero-width characters from the model input and record the transformation. Accept: property test I5 (paragraph count and order); fixtures with surrogate pairs, combining marks, 50,000-character paragraph. Estimate: 3 to 4 h. Depends: T3.1. Owner: agent.

**T3.3 Write the output validators.** Why: sanitization s4, FP-4, FP-D2, FP-D3, FP-5. Steps: `src/lib/translate/validate.ts` with the seven checks in the specified order, linear-time (no regex that can backtrack; use character scans like `src/lib/search/scan.ts`), thresholds from config, reason codes from T1.2; reuse `detectInjection` for check 7. Accept: unit tests for every fake mode; microbenchmark under 50 ms per 100 KB for ar, zh, en (HP-D1). Estimate: 3 to 4 h. Depends: T3.2. Owner: agent; human reviews the patterns and thresholds.

**T3.4 Add the OpenAI translate adapter and the mock.** Why: ADR-0023, ADR-0013, C12. Treat a unique-index conflict as already done only when the stored `enrichment_id`/version match. Where: `src/worker/finish.ts`, `src/worker/loop.ts`. Accept: tests I2, I3, I4, I7, I8, I9, I10 pass, including the 50x50 concurrency repetition. Estimate: 3.5 to 5 h. Depends: T3.4. Owner: agent, human review.

Accept: `fail_on_chunk(7)` retry calls only chunks 7..n and ends with the same text hash as a clean run. Estimate: 3 to 4 h. Depends: T4.1. Owner: agent.

## 1. Summary
Build: for non-English articles, translate headline and body to English at ingest through a third enrichment part, show the translation by default with a "Show original" toggle, and make search match both texts. Eight phases, about 90 to 120 hours in total (large uncertainty in the worker and UI phases, section 8). Critical path: schema (P1) → enqueue (P2) → worker lane core (P3) → save, cache and budget (P4) → UI (P6) → hardening (P8). Search (P5) and telemetry (P7) can run in parallel after P4's save path exists.

## 6. Phases

### Phase 1: Decisions, helpers, configuration and schema (≈10 to 14 h)
Goal: the database has the translation schema and the code has configuration and shared helpers, with nothing yet enqueued.
Entry: B2 answered (T1.1). 
Exit: `0004` applies cleanly on an empty database and on a populated one, re-applies safely, rollback dry-run works; config validates; unit tests for helpers pass.
Rollback/safe-stop: nothing behaves differently until P2; dropping the new tables restores the old state.
Human checkpoints: T1.1 (decision), review of the migration (T1.4).

**T1.1 Resolve B2 and record it.** Why: ADR-0010, spend control (P2). Steps: ask the user B2; if a decision is made, record an ADR via carma-architect; set the defaults in T1.3 accordingly. Where: `.specs/architect/adrs/`. Accept: ADR number noted in the plan. Estimate: 0.5 to 1 h. Depends: none. Owner: human (decision). Specs: devops 0003 s6, sanitization 0003 s9.

**T1.2 Add shared translation helpers.** Why: single source of truth for the language rule and reason codes (C5, C13). Steps: create `src/lib/translate/language.ts` (`isEnglish`, `needsTranslation`), `src/lib/translate/reasons.ts` (enum with job reason, metric label, UI copy key), types for the translation part; extend `src/lib/reasons.ts` if it already holds reason codes (read it first). Where: `src/lib/translate/*`, `tests/unit/translate-language.test.ts`. Accept: table tests for `en`, `EN`, `en-GB`, `en_US`, `eng`, `ar`, `zh-Hans`, empty, null, `"N/A"`; reasons enum covers all sanitization and telemetry codes. Estimate: 1.5 to 2.5 h. Depends: T1.1. Owner: agent. Specs: search/sanitization 0003 s3, UX s5.

**T1.3 Add configuration.** Why: devops 0003 s6. Steps: add the variables to the zod schema in `src/lib/config.ts` with ranges (`TRANSLATE_RATIO_*` parsed from "min,max", min < max), add to the typed config object, `.env.example`, `compose.yaml` worker env (and `compose.dev.yaml` if it duplicates env), `docs/environment.md`; add `script` and `view` to `ALLOWED_LABEL_KEYS` and update `tests/unit/metrics-labels.test.ts` and `tests/unit/config.test.ts`. Where: `src/lib/config.ts`, `src/lib/metrics.ts`, `.env.example`, `compose*.yaml`, `docs/environment.md`. Accept: bad values fail with the variable name; defaults match devops 0003 s6; `ENRICHMENT_MODE=real` without a key still fails fast. Estimate: 1.5 to 2.5 h. Depends: T1.2. Owner: agent.

**T1.4 Write migration `0004_article_translations.sql`.** Why: DBA 0003 s4, s7, s10. Steps: (1) drop and re-add the two `part` CHECKs, looking constraint names up in `pg_constraint`, using `NOT VALID` then `VALIDATE`; (2) create `article_translations` with the columns in DBA 0003 s4 (no confidence columns), the CHECK `at_has_text`, `fillfactor 90`, autovacuum settings; (3) partial unique index `article_translations_current_uq`, partial GIN on `search_vector`, partial trigram GIN guarded by the `trgm_index` flag (same pattern as `0001_init.sql:179-188`), built `CONCURRENTLY` is not possible inside the migration transaction, so create it with the table (empty); (4) `translation_chunk_cache`; (5) grants from DBA 0003 s10 (app_read SELECT on `article_translations`, app_worker SELECT/INSERT plus `UPDATE (superseded_at)`, cache table to app_worker only); (6) seed `system_flags` `translation_enabled` from the setting in `src/cli/migrate.ts` next to `enrichment_enabled`; (7) write the manual rollback as a comment block at the top like `0003`. Where: `db/migrations/0004_article_translations.sql`, `src/cli/migrate.ts`. Accept: applies on an empty database and on a database at `0003` with data; second run is a no-op; `\d` shows the indexes; grants verified by attempting forbidden writes as each role. Estimate: 3 to 4 h. Depends: T1.3. Owner: agent, human review (migration review). Specs: DBA 0003 s4, s7, s10; devops s5.

**T1.5 Test the migration.** Why: FP-DB3, FP-DB6. Steps: integration test applying `0003` then `0004` on a seeded database; check constraints, indexes, grants per role, idempotent re-run; a test that the migration file contains no non-concurrent index creation on existing populated tables (static grep); measure the constraint swap with 1M job rows (run once, record the lock time, `tests/integration/migration-0004.test.ts`). Accept: lock time under 1 s at 1M rows. Estimate: 2.5 to 3.5 h. Depends: T1.4. Owner: agent. Specs: testing 0003 FP-DB3, devops s9.

### Phase 4: Save path, cache, budget and fault handling (≈11 to 15 h)
Goal: an article is translated end to end and the result is stored safely.
Entry: P3 exit.
Exit: I1 to I10 pass; budget, breaker, kill switch and crash tests pass; carma-review done.
Rollback/safe-stop: kill switch `translation_enabled=false`.

**T4.1 Implement the save transaction.** Why: FP-6, FP-DB2, DBA 0003 s8, C7. Steps: `finishTranslation` in `src/worker/finish.ts`: begin; take `pg_advisory_xact_lock(hashtext('article'), article_id)`; re-check `articles.version`; if changed mark job `superseded_version` and stop; supersede any current translation; insert `enrichments` (`part='translation'`, `raw_output = {usage, model_reported, chunk_count}` only, trust `low` when the injection flag was set); insert `article_translations` with `search_text` from the shared normaliser (`src/lib/normalise`, `search_text_ver`); mark job `succeeded`; delete cache rows; commit. Treat a unique-index conflict as already done only when the stored `enrichment_id`/version match. Where: `src/worker/finish.ts`, `src/worker/loop.ts`. Accept: tests I2, I3, I4, I7, I8, I9, I10 pass, including the 50x50 concurrency repetition. Estimate: 3.5 to 5 h. Depends: T3.4. Owner: agent, human review.

**T4.2 Implement the chunk cache and the job runner.** Why: I6, FP-D4. Steps: `processTranslationJob` in `loop.ts`: reserve the budget for all chunks up front; for each chunk check `translation_chunk_cache` by `(job_id, chunk_idx, input_hash)`; call provider; validate; write the cache row in its own small transaction; join; validate whole; save; release the reservation on failure. Failure classes via `classifyProviderError` and `maxAttemptsFor`; invalid output has 2 attempts; `too_long` is dead immediately. Accept: `fail_on_chunk(7)` retry calls only chunks 7..n and ends with the same text hash as a clean run. Estimate: 3 to 4 h. Depends: T4.1. Owner: agent.

Accept: exhausting the translate cap leaves sentiment/summary lanes unaffected; fake clock moves to the next UTC day and jobs resume; breaker opens/half-opens per `tests/unit/breaker.test.ts` semantics. Estimate: 2 to 3 h. Depends: T4.1. Owner: agent.

**T4.4 Extend the sweeper and the kill switch.** Why: FP-DB5, ADR-0022. Steps: `sweepExpired` also purges cache rows older than `TRANSLATE_CACHE_DAYS` after a terminal job, deletes superseded translations older than `TRANSLATE_SUPERSEDED_DAYS`; `translation_enabled` flag read each loop; status snapshot exposes translation job counts. Accept: sweeper tests with the fake clock; flag off stops claims, flag on drains. Estimate: 1.5 to 2.5 h. Depends: T4.1. Owner: agent.

**T4.5 Write worker integration and fault tests, then gate.** Why: testing 0003 s4, s8.1. Accept: all section 8.3 cases pass; counts equal a direct SQL count. Estimate: 3 to 4 h. Depends: T5.3. Owner: agent.
